entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Green Dragon Wyrmling Breath
entries: This can be harvested from a {@creature Green Dragon Wyrmling||wyrmling green dragon} or a Medium size (or smaller) green half-dragon. A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw. The creature takes 21 ({@damage 6d6}) poison damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful save.

name: Green Slime
entries: Green slime appears as a viscous green mass with weak acidic properties. Healers favor green slime as an unguent in topical ointments. Howlers often keep globules of green slime tucked in their cheeks. The substance green slime is cultivated from larger, living omnivorous monsters of the same name.

name: Greenblood Oil
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute.

name: Grell Venom
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. While {@condition poisoned}, the target is {@condition paralyzed}. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a success.

name: Grenade
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Grenade
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Grenade Launcher
entries: This weapon allows you to propel a {@item fragmentation|MH}, {@item smoke|MH} or {@item tear gas|MH} grenade up to 120 feet away. You can target a creature instead using a grenade launcher. On a hit you deal {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage to that creature, and then the grenade effect occurs.

name: Grululu
entries: The grululu is a larger, two-handed variant of the {@item ululu|BloodInTheCompany} played by professional musicians. Much like the {@item ululu|BloodInTheCompany}, it can be played by striking along its length with a baton or by hitting hostile enemies (or volunteers) with it. Due to its extended length, the grululu has a greater variety of notes and tones it can play. Due to its rarity and craftsmanship it is a serious investment for musicians.

name: Grung Sweat
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or become {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. A {@condition poisoned} creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a success.

name: Guardian Naga Venom
entries: A creature subjected to this poison takes (45) {@damage 10d8} poison damage.

name: Guardian Spear
entries: A slightly misleading name for the formidable weapon wielded by a {@creature Knight-Guardian of the Lightning Lord|FFESLL}, this polearm resembles a glaive with a strange arcane device capable of projecting blasts of lightning mounted next to the blade.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon is considered adamantine for the purposes of resistance and immunity.

entries.name: Ranged Attack
entries: This weapon may also make ranged attacks in the same manner as a ranged weapon, which deal 4d8 lightning damage.

When fired, a bolt of lightning forming a line 100 feet long (or the lesser distance between the firer and the target) and 5 feet wide blasts out from the Guardian Spear. On a hit each creature in the line that isn't the target must make a Dexterity saving throw, with a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier. A creature takes the weapon's damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
When used as a ranged weapon it has the following additional properties:

name: Guisarme
entries: {@i A spiked polearm with a blade that curves dramatically over, forming a hook.}

name: Gunlance
entries: Gunlances take the form of one-handed polearms with built-in short-range firearms. They also have the Special: Point Blank property and the {@itemMastery Piercing Shot|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms|Piercing Shot Superior Strike}{@sup *}, with a range of 30 feet.

entries.name: Special: Point Blank
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while wielding this weapon, you can prime it for shooting. The next time you hit with a melee attack using this weapon before the end of your turn, the attack deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Thunder damage.
{@note {@sup *}See {@loader Ryoko's Guide to the Yokai Realms|collection/Loot Tavern; Ryoko's Guide to Yokai Realms.json}}

name: Gunpowder Keg
entries: 100 doses of powder

name: Gyrspike
entries: {@i A long-handled sword with a chain and spiked ball attached to the handle.}
{@note The Tripping property applies only to the 2nd side, which deals {@damage 1d4} bludgeoning damage.}

name: Gythka
entries: {@i A short-length polearm with a slashing blade at each end. Traditional gythka blades are made of crystal, but metal is also used.}

name: Gythka
entries: A dual-bladed polearm of thri-kreen origin. You can also use this as a template for a Double-Axe, Double- Hammer, or Double-Spear, which deal slashing, bludgeoning, and piercing damage.

entries.name: Weapon Technique
entries: {@optfeature Double Weapon|MATM}: A gythka is a double weapon. You can use your bonus action to change stances and fight with it as if fighting with two light one-handed weapons. When wielded normally the gythka's damage die is {@damage 1d10}, but when double weapon fighting the weapon's damage die becomes {@damage 1d6}.

entries.name: Weapon Technique
entries: {@optfeature Sweep|MATM}: When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn with a gythka against a large or smaller creature, you can sweep an enemy's legs out from under them with your gythka. If the attack hits, the attack causes no damage or other ill effect, but the creature must make a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone}. You can only use this technique once per turn.

name: Gythka
entries: {@i A short-length polearm with a slashing blade at each end. Traditional gythka blades are made of crystal, but metal is also used.}

name: Hakuma Sapwood
entries: Hakuma sapwood is a fragrant and combustible wood that comes from the center of the hakuma tree. It is burned at shrines and sacred sites throughout Obojima, delivering a complex and pleasing incense that clears the mind and soothes the soul. Hakuma trees are quite common across the island, but unless you are a priest, a druid, or know the proper rituals, most Obojimans frown on taking limbs from these trees.

name: Hakumon's Ramen Broth
entries: The ramen broth made by master ramen chef, Hakumon, is legendary among chefs and potion makers alike for its particularly potent effects. Many ramen competitors and potion makers have been known to pay a high price to secure a container-full of broth from Hakumon's famed ramen shop. But be warned! For Hakumon, ramen is no laughing matter, and the master chef takes great pains to ensure that thieves and miscreants cannot steal his broth so easily.

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Hallucinogenic Myconid Spore
entries: This poison is collected as a spore, not stored in a glass vial. When burst by an impact, the spore fills a 20-feet cube. A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. The {@condition poisoned} target is {@condition incapacitated} while it hallucinates. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Haluroot
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 9} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Wisdom)} for 1 minute.

name: Hanbō
entries: A short quarterstaff.

entries.name: Wooden Ammunition
entries: Wooden ammunition is destroyed after hitting or missing a target.

name: Hand Culverin
entries: {@i A wide-mouthed handgun often used for peppering close enemies. It is designed to allow shot loads to spread at a close range. Dragons are common firearms for horse soldiers, giving rise to the name "dragoon."}
This weapon loads shot only.

name: Hand culverin
entries: A short-barreled version of the arquebus, fired while the notched butt rests on the shoulder. This weapon has a very wide barrel, used for firing clusters of pellets at short range.
This weapon loads shot only.

name: Hand of Eryo
entries: These extremely rare mushrooms are the most desired of all the edible mushrooms on Obojima. They tend to grow in the uppermost branches, where they appear to be grasping at the sky. Forest spirits who locate one of these mushrooms will descend on it with ravenous frenzy, so foragers who hope to harvest some of their own might find stiff competition.

name: Hand Razors
entries: {@i A series of rings, sometimes attached to one another, that fit over the fingers of one hand. Small, sharp blades are affixed to the rings. In combat, these are positioned upward, protruding from the knuckles or downward, concealed within the palm of the hand. They are often used to deliver poisons.}

name: Hand razors
entries: A series of rings, sometimes attached to one another, that fit over the fingers of one hand. Small, sharp blades are affixed to the rings. In combat, these are positioned upward, protruding from the knuckles or downward, concealed within the palm of the hand. They are often used to deliver poisons.

name: Hand Tommybow (2)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Hand Tommybow (3)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Hand Tommybow (4)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Hand Tommybow (5)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Hand Tommybow (6)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

entries.name: Special
entries: The metal pocket of a hand trebuchet can be loaded with {@item acid (vial)|PHB|a small container of acid}, {@item alchemist's fire (flask)|PHB|alchemist's fire}, {@item holy water (flask)|PHB|holy water}, or other liquid. See the appropriate entry for the ammunition used to determine damage and other effects. As a melee weapon, a hand trebuchet deals damage as a {@item club|PHB}.

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Handgonne
entries: {@i A simple firearm consisting of a short tube mounted at the end of a rod.}
This weapon loads ball only.

name: Handgonne
entries: A simple firearm consisting of a short tube mounted at the end of a rod.
This weapon loads ball only.

name: Handgun
entries: Portable, reliable, and with a generous magazine size, the Handgun is the go-to firearm for self-defense and law enforcement.

name: Hankyu
entries: {@i A common weapon in most cultures, this consists of a springy stock or haft, bent into a bow shape by a shorter string connected to both ends. Holding the middle of the bow and pulling the string back increases the weapon's tension; when the string is released, the recoil can rapidly project a missile attached to the string, pushing it past the bow. A hankyu has a shorter length relative to a daikyu, better suited for mounted use.}

name: Hankyū
entries: A shortbow.

name: Happy Joy Cake
entries: The makers of Happy Joy Cake are a secretive family and it is believed that at least one of them is a spirit, but Obojimans are nevertheless in love with the small, bite-sized treats whose recipe has been handed down for generations. Although Happy Joy Cakes are made only in Yatamon, there are a few trusted traveling merchants who are allowed to distribute them across the island.

name: Haramaki
entries: {@i A series of very-dense lacquered plates, interlocking in a suit that covers the torso, tying in the back.}

name: Hardened Mail Shirt
entries: This chain shirt has rings of adamantine or mithral woven into key areas to provide more protection than normal mail.

name: Hardlight Dart
entries: Glowing in scintillating hardlight, the Hardlight Dart is a magical projectile that shatters and radiates away seconds after impacting its target. Such darts are inexpensive and disposable, favored by assassins.

name: Harp
entries: {@i A harp has many parallel strings attached within a frame. The frame has an angled soundboard that facilitates shorter strings as it tapers, varying the notes produced when the instrument is strummed.}

name: Harpoon
entries: {@i A harpoon is a thrown weapon designed to impale its target. A trailing rope restricts the target's movement after the weapon binds in the target's flesh.}

Despite its standard range increments, a harpoon cannot be used to attack a creature that is farther away than the length of its attached rope. These special rules apply only if the harpoon is attached to such a trailing rope; otherwise treat the weapon in all ways as a {@item javelin|CompEquipMan}.

A harpoon attack that inflicts at least 5 damage binds the target. A harpooned creature is {@condition restrained} except that it can still move its normal speed, provided it goes no further away from the attacker. This range can be shortened over time if the other end of the rope is attached to a winch.

A harpooned creature can use its action to make a Strength check to free itself from the weapon. The DC is 10, or the damage inflicted by the harpoon attack, whichever is higher. A creature with an Intelligence of 7 or higher automatically succeeds at this check, understanding innately how to manipulate the weapon to free itself.

Alternately, the creature can attempt to pull free, dragging the weapon and rope with it. If you control the other end of the rope, this is an opposed check of Strength ({@skill Athletics}). If the creature is two or more sizes larger than you, this check succeeds automatically. If the rope is tied to an object, the creature must instead try to burst the rope or drag the attached object.

entries.name: Special
entries: You can use an action to tie a rope to the end of a harpoon before it is thrown. If a rope-tied harpoon hits a target, it becomes embedded in the target, and you can use an action on subsequent turns to hold fast to the rope and make an opposed Strength (Athletics) check against the target to pull it up to 10 feet closer to you. Additionally, when the target moves, you can use your reaction to make an opposed Strength (Athletics) check against it, preventing its movement on a success. If you use your action to do anything else, you lose your grip on the rope. If the target has hands, it can remove the harpoon as an action.

name: Hatchet
entries: {@i This weapon resembles a handaxe with a smaller, un-bearded blade and a lighter handle.}

name: Hatchet
entries: {@i This weapon resembles a handaxe with a smaller, un-bearded blade and a lighter handle.}

name: Hauberk
entries: A hauberk is a shirt of mail that reaches at least to mid-thigh and includes sleeves.

name: Hayokpe
entries: A leather laminar armor with ankle-length skirts, worn by the hunters of Rep-un-Mosir.

name: Heater Shield
entries: If the wearer has a Strength score lower than 13, their speed is reduced by 10 feet.

entries.name: Special
entries: You have disadvantage on attacks made with a bayonet that isn't attached to a crossbow. It takes an action to attach or remove a bayonet from a weapon.

name: Heavy Cannon
entries: Ballistic weapons are uncommon in space combat, but not totally unheard of (and certainly not ineffective). A heavy cannon fires {@item Heavy Cannon Round|DarkMatter|large-diameter explosive shells}, which unlike blaster bolts, must lead their target to account for travel time.

entries.name: Wooden Ammunition
entries: Wooden ammunition is destroyed after hitting or missing a target.

entries.name: Special
entries: Each creature in a 30-foot cone must make a Dexterity saving throw, with a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier. A creature takes {@damage 2d8} plus your dexterity modifier in fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The fire ignites any flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.

name: Heavy Gauntlet
entries: A large reinforced gauntlet, designed to channel and enhance every mote of the user's strength.

entries.name: Special
entries: If hit and affected by the damage, they must make a Constitution saving throw, with a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier, or be {@condition stunned} until the end of their next turn.

name: Heavy Leather Armor
entries: The centerpiece of a set of heavy leather armor is its fitted chest, boiled, molded, and hardened in the image of a muscled torso. Such armor often incorporates studded leather tassets that hang down for further protection. Such armor may be simple with little detail, or ornate with bronze motifs.

name: Heavy Mace
entries: {@i This weapon has a longer handle and heavier head than the normal mace.}

name: Heavy Mace
entries: {@i This weapon has a longer handle and heavier head than the normal mace.}

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d4} piercing damage on a hit or an additional {@damage 1d6} piercing damage if used with both hands.

name: Heavy Pistol
entries: {@i A larger version of a standard pistol, this weapon trades ease of handling for additional stopping power.}
This weapon loads (magnum) cartridges.

entries.name: Special
entries: You require a Strength score of 13 to use this weapon effectively, else your attacks have disadvantage.
Additionally you are unable to use a shield whilst holding this weapon in one hand.

name: Heavy Slingshot
entries: The heavy slingshot is a weapon used primarily by Huascan soldiers. It is a large, cumbersome weapon that utilises very powerful elastic natural rubbers to propel {@item Sling Bullet|PHB|bullets} at long distances.

name: Heavy Tommybow (2)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Heavy Tommybow (3)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Heavy Tommybow (6)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Helmet
entries: The effects of a helmet are included in armor, this entry is largely to allow for standalone helmet creation for enchanters.

name: Heraldic Shield
entries: This fine shield bears an emblem or coat of arms associated with an organization, such as a knightly order or civil guard, the faith of a particular god, or a location, such as your country of origin. While you visibly carry this shield, you have advantage on Charisma checks to interact with members of the shield's displayed affiliation.

name: Herbalism Kit
entries: This kit contains a variety of instruments such as clippers, mortar and pestle, and pouches and vials used by herbalists to create remedies and potions. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to identify or apply herbs. Also, proficiency with this kit is required to create antitoxin and potions of healing.

If you are proficient with the herbalism kit, during each Fellowship Phase you can collect medicinal plants and use them to create a number of herbal remedies equal to your proficiency bonus, or twice as much if a feature lets you add double your proficiency bonus with the herbalism kit.
A remedy can be expended to gain advantage on an Intelligence ({@skill Medicine}) check, or it can be consumed as an action to gain advantage on saving throws against disease and poison for 1 hour.

name: Heroic Cuirass
entries: A fitted bronze breastplate and backplate, sculpted to depict the stylized musculature of the chest and abdomen of the warrior beneath. Such armor often incorporates studded tassets that hang down for further protection.

name: Heroic Panoply
entries: This full set of bronze armor consists of multiple pieces centred around a heroic cuirass. It includes bronze bracers and greaves as well as a corinthian helm, sometimes crested with a plume of bristling horse hair.

name: Hichiriki
entries: {@i The pitch of this double-reed flute is controlled with mouth positioning, allowing a variety of bended notes.}

name: Hidden Blade
entries: {@i This small, spring-loaded blade can be hidden in various objects. It is often hidden in stiff articles of clothing, like a leather bracer or the sole of a boot, but it can also be hidden at the end of a staff, at the bottom of a shield, or inside various innocuous tools.}

A hidden blade can be drawn (or revealed by a spring-loaded mechanism) as an action or a bonus action. This typically requires some complex adjustment of the item in order to reveal the blade. Some versions remain attached to the objects they were concealed in; others are drawn free like a knife.

One classic example of a hidden blade is called a "toe spike." This blade is concealed in the sole of a boot and "drawn" by pressing the heal sideways into the ground, causing the blade to appear, projecting from the toe of the boot.

A hidden blade is an improvised weapon that closely resembles a small dagger. It inflicts {@damage 1d4} piercing damage in combat. The DM decides if a weapon proficiency bonus applies, depending on where the blade is attached; at the end of a pole, the weapon might closely resemble a {@item spear|CompEquipMan}, a version that projects from a bracer might resemble a {@item punch dagger|CompEquipMan|punching dagger}, and a version that draws clear might be a normal {@item dagger|CompEquipMan}.

name: Hidden Blade
entries: {@i This small, spring-loaded blade can be hidden in various objects. It is often hidden in stiff articles of clothing, like a leather bracer or the sole of a boot, but it can also be hidden at the end of a staff, at the bottom of a shield, or inside various innocuous tools.}

entries.name: Special
entries: A hidden blade can be drawn (or revealed by a spring-loaded mechanism) as an action or a bonus action. This typically requires some complex adjustment of the item in order to reveal the blade. Some versions remain attached to the objects they were concealed in; others are drawn free like a knife.

One classic example of a hidden blade is called a "toe spike." This blade is concealed in the sole of a boot and "drawn" by pressing the heal sideways into the ground, causing the blade to appear, projecting from the toe of the boot.

A hidden blade is an improvised weapon that closely resembles a small dagger. It inflicts {@dice 1d4} piercing damage in combat. The DM decides if a weapon proficiency bonus applies, depending on where the blade is attached; at the end of a pole, the weapon might closely resemble a spear, a version that projects from a bracer might resemble a punching dagger, and a version that draws clear might be a normal dagger.

name: Hide
entries: Used for {@book Leatherworking|KTKCG|17}.

name: Hide Scraps
entries: Used for {@book Leatherworking|KTKCG|17}.

name: Hill Dragon Egg
entries: Looking like pumpkin-sized acorns, hill dragon eggs can remain dormant in the ground for a year or more before they hatch. Hill dragon eggs are usually buried out of sight, but certain flowers like to grow around burial pits giving their positions away and egg-hunting hogs can be trained to sniff them out. Not known for powerful maternal instincts, hill dragons lay their eggs in clutches all across the plains, dales, and rolling hills of Obojima.

name: Hnefatafl Set
entries: {@i A strategy game played on a checkered or latticed board between two unevenly-matched armies of carved figures.}

name: Holy Water (Flask)
entries: {@i This water has a glittery sheen, a byproduct of the ingredients used to create it.}

As an action, you can splash the contents of this flask onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw it up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against the target creature, treating the holy water as an improvised weapon. If the target is a fiend or undead, and the attack hits, the holy water inflicts {@damage 2d6} radiant damage.

A cleric or paladin may create holy water by performing a special ritual. The ritual takes one hour, uses 25 gp worth of powdered silver, and requires the caster to expend a 1st-level spell slot. The Dungeon Master may instead require this ritual to be prepared and cast as a {@spell ceremony|XGE} spell.

name: Homunculus Saliva
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the target is instead {@condition poisoned} for 1d10 minutes and is {@condition unconscious} while {@condition poisoned} this way.

name: Hook
entries: {@i Hooks are often attached to handles to serve as tools for lifting bales of hay. They can also serve as weapons. In certain cultures, hooks on cinched caps are common prostheses for lost hands.}

name: Hook
entries: {@i Hooks are often attached to handles to serve as tools for lifting bales of hay. They can also serve as weapons. In certain cultures, hooks on cinched caps are common prostheses for lost hands.}

entries.name: Special
entries: This is a one-handed weapon, usable only if you are missing a hand or have a special cuff designed to fit over your hand. Any humanoid that is missing a hand and regularly wears a hook has proficiency with this weapon.

name: Hooked Blowgun Needle (50)
entries: {@i This blowgun needle has several small hooks behind the tip that make it hard to remove from the target.}
This applies the cruel weapon property to attacks made with it.

name: Hooked Blowgun Needle
entries: {@i This blowgun needle has several small hooks behind the tip that make it hard to remove from the target.}
This applies the cruel weapon property to attacks made with it.

name: Hooked Hammer
entries: {@i This war pick has a hammer head at the opposite end of the handle.}
{@note The Tripping property applies only to the 2nd side, which deals {@damage 1d4} piercing damage.}

name: Hooked Shortspear
entries: {@i The backward-facing hook on this short-hafted spear is designed for tripping opponents. Some versions have a smaller opposite hook on the butt end.}

entries.name: Special
entries: Once per turn, you may make one of your attacks with this weapon a trap. If the attack misses you grapple the target and may immediately make a hilt spike attack with advantage against it. This attack deals {@damage 1d4} piercing damage on a hit.
However if the trapped attack hits, it deals no damage.

entries.name: Special
entries: Once per turn, you may make one of your attacks with this weapon a trap. If the attack misses you grapple the target and may immediately make a hilt spike attack with advantage against it. This attack deals {@damage 1d4} piercing damage on a hit.
However if the trapped attack hits, it deals no damage.

name: Hooksword
entries: Hookswords are wielded to trip opponents, but when used as a pair they can hook together to extend their reach to slash at foes from a distance.

entries.name: Weapon Technique
entries: {@optfeature Blade-Link|MATM}: If you are wielding two hookswords, you can use your bonus action to hook them together at their ends. While linked in this way, the two hookswords become a single two-handed weapon with the Reach property that deals {@damage 1d10} slashing damage on hit.

entries.name: Weapon Technique
entries: {@optfeature Sweep|MATM}: While your sword(s) are not linked and you make a melee weapon attack on your turn with a hooksword against a large or smaller creature, you can sweep an enemy's legs out from under them with the hook of your blade. If the attack hits, the attack causes no damage or other ill effect, but the creature must make a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone}. You can only use this technique once per turn.

name: Horagai
entries: {@i A large conch shell with a metal mouthpiece, this instrument is used like a trumpet.}

name: Horror Weed Extract
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Wisdom)} for 24 hours. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each hour, ending the effect on itself with a success. Each failed saving throw inflicts 2 ({@damage 1d4}) psychic damage that cannot be healed until the {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned} condition is removed. This substance can be perceived as magical (no school) using a {@spell detect magic} spell or similar effect.

name: Horseman's War Pick
entries: {@i This pick has an extra-long handle, suitable for use on horseback, or for infantry reaching and dragging a knight down from a horse.}

name: Horseman's Warpick
entries: {@i This pick has an extra-long handle, suitable for use on horseback, or for infantry reaching and dragging a knight down from a horse.}

name: Horseshoe
entries: Shoes for horses.

name: Horseshoes (set of 4)
entries: Shoes (4) for horses.

name: Hoshi
entries: {@i This elaborate helmet flares widely at the back to protect the neck and shoulders. A fearsome mask covers the face and tall protrusions, or ornamentations complete the intimidating appearance.}

Wearing a hoshi helmet grants immunity to the special mechanics of saps and garrotes. It provides a +2 bonus to the wearer's Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks but gives the wearer's Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks disadvantage.

name: Hotchiku
entries: {@i A long flute made from a single piece of heavy bamboo, collected from the root-end of the stalk.}
This heavy instrument can be used as a {@item club|CompEquipMan}.

name: Hotoke
entries: {@i This solid breastplate and back plate of lacquered metal are typically joined by joints on one side and tied closed along the other side to encase the torso. Smaller sets of plates cover the joints.}

name: Howdah Pistol
entries: {@i A heavy, four-barreled breach-loading pistol designed to stop large animals.}
This weapon loads (carbine) cartridges.

name: Howler Fur
entries: Howler fur has certain arcane properties that are sought after by witches and warlocks for their various brews. Some Obojimans believe that a tuft of howler fur that is burned in a fireplace can ward off evil spirits. Howler fur can be found snagged on bramble thickets, along game trails, and near howler camps within and around the forests and caves where they dwell.

name: Hunting Rifle
entries: Designed for big game, Hunting Rifles are slow but accurate, requiring bolt action operation between every shot.

name: Hyoshigi
entries: {@i This solid breastplate and back plate of lacquered metal are typically joined by joints on one side and tied closed along the other side to encase the torso. Smaller sets of plates cover the joints.}

name: Icesteel Ingot
entries: Used for {@book Blacksmithing|KTKCG|12}.

name: Icesteel Ore
entries: Smelting ore requires specialized factilities. This can usually be accomplished in a fully equiped smithy, but consult your GM for where it might be appropriate. Adventurers rarely smelt their own ore, these are included primarily for informational purposes. Smelting magical ores may require more specialized facilities or locations.

name: Id Moss
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Intelligence)} for 24 hours. While the condition persists, the victim suffers disadvantage on saving throws based on Intelligence. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each hour, ending the effect on itself with a success.

name: Imp Sting
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw, taking 11 ({@damage 3d6}) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful save.

entries.name: Special
entries: On a hit this weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d12} radiant damage.

name: Inking Crossbow Bolt
entries: {@i This heavy crossbow bolt bears a large, spongy head soaked in bright ink. The bolt is typically carried inside a wax coating that covers the head to preserve the ink prior to use. Such bolts are often used by spotters in battle to mark certain targets. By prearranged agreement, this focuses the attention of allied ranged units like archers and war wizards.}

The wax coating on the head of this bolt can be removed as a bonus action during loading, making it ready to fire. Anything the missile hits is splattered with the bright ink. A crossbow firing an inking crossbow bolt reduces its damage to {@damage 1d2} bludgeoning.
Because of their shape, these bolts cannot be loaded into a {@item repeating crossbow|CompEquipMan} magazine.

name: Insanity Smoke
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Wisdom)} for 1 hour. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each minute, ending the effect on itself with a success. Each failed saving throw inflicts 4 ({@damage 1d8}) psychic damage that cannot be healed until the {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned} condition is removed. This substance can be perceived as magical (no school) using a {@spell detect magic} spell or similar effect.

name: Ion Cannon
entries: The ion cannon always fires in a bright, diffuse cone, making it far deadlier up close. Between shots, it always makes a quiet zipping noise, as the arcane battery charges the ion cell for another blast.

name: Ion Cannon
entries: The Ion Cannon fires a bright, diffuse cone, rendering it deadly up close. Between shots, it makes a quiet zipping noise, as the arcane battery charges the ion cell for another blast.

name: Ion Cannon
entries: The Ion Cannon fires a bright, diffuse cone, rendering it deadly up close. Between shots, it makes a quiet zipping noise, as the arcane battery charges the ion cell for another blast.

name: Ion Cannon
entries: The Ion Cannon fires a bright, diffuse cone, rendering it deadly up close. Between shots, it makes a quiet zipping noise, as the arcane battery charges the ion cell for another blast.

name: Irimbi Chrysalis
entries: Every ten years, deep in the forests of Obojima, the rare irimbi caterpillar climbs to the highest branches to make a jade-green chrysalis in which it transforms into an irimbi butterfly. The chrysalis feels like delicate rice paper to the touch, and finding one intact is almost impossible due to tree mites, which tend to make quick work of their favorite meal.

name: Iron Golem Fumes
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 19} Constitution saving throw. The creature takes 45 ({@damage 10d8}) poison damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful save.

name: Iron Ingot
entries: Used for {@book Blacksmithing|KTKCG|12}.

name: Itchi Beri
entries: Itchi berries can be harvested in clusters from under the vibrant green leaves of the Itchi plant, which are known to cause severe rashes on exposed skin. The berries themselves are harmless and sweeten when reduced to a jam. Itchi plants are most often found on riverbanks, their leaves pointing toward the peak of Mount Arbora. Sages have speculated about this phenomenon for generations, but no conclusive evidence has laid the matter to rest.

name: Jack-O'-Lantern Bits
entries: Many witches say that the process of carving a jack-o'-lantern bestows a certain amount of magic into the pumpkin, and lighting a candle within it absorbs the energy of the special time of the fall season when most witches agree that magic is at its most potent. Thus, pieces of a jack-o'-lantern are imbued with eldritch energies that are key to certain potions and magics.

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wooden Melee Weapons
entries: When you make an attack roll with this Melee weapon and roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, the weapon splinters and is destroyed.

name: Jitte
entries: {@i A metal rod tapering to a dull point, with one parallel prong curving forward from the handle.}

name: Jitte
entries: A thin steel baton with a hook at the hilt used for disarming

entries.name: Special
entries: When you attack with this weapon, you can choose whether the damage is piercing or bludgeoning. Then, you can use a bonus action to {@action disarm|dmg} a target.

name: Johyo
entries: {@i This heavy dart is attached to the end of a 15-foot, lightweight rope.}

This can be swung to make melee attacks against foes within five feet or it can be thrown up to 15 feet. When thrown, a proficient wielder keeps ahold of the end of the rope and, as part of the attack, can whip the dart back into the hand after a throw.

name: Joining Dirks (joined)
entries: Interlocking pommels cap this pair of blades.

entries.name: Special
entries: As a bonus action, you can interlock the pommels to create a single weapon with a blade on each end, and you can use a bonus action while holding the joined blade to separate it into the two blades again. When the blades are joined, this weapon has the {@bold double-headed} ({@damage 1d6}) and {@bold two-handed} properties, and it loses the {@bold light} property. When the blades are separate, you have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) checks to hide them on your person.

name: Joining Dirks (separate)
entries: Interlocking pommels cap this pair of blades.

entries.name: Special
entries: As a bonus action, you can interlock the pommels to create a single weapon with a blade on each end, and you can use a bonus action while holding the joined blade to separate it into the two blades again. When the blades are joined, this weapon has the {@bold double-headed} ({@damage 1d6}) and {@bold two-handed} properties, and it loses the {@bold light} property. When the blades are separate, you have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) checks to hide them on your person.

name: Jotunskull Helm
entries: Favored by those who wish to project a fearsome aspect, these helms are fashioned from the cleaned bones of a sufficiently large giant. When you wear one, you have Advantage on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks against Giants (at the GM's discretion).

name: Jousting Lance
entries: A jousting lance has a blunt end and is made to break away on impact. A creature wearing heavy armor has resistance to damage inflicted by a jousting lance.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon is too large to use unless affixed to an exotic saddle or howdah on a Huge-size (or larger) creature. This weapon has a 15-foot reach. You have disadvantage when you use a great lance to attack a target within 10 feet of you.

name: Jūmonji-yari
entries: A three-pronged yari spear.

name: Jumping Bonfire
entries: This brightly colored flower is well-known throughout Obojima for the unique way that it propagates its seeds. When the flower of a jumping bonfire plant is knocked by a passerby, its petals begin to wriggle about mimicking flames and the seeds within it shoot out from the central stem with an audible popping sound like logs cracking on a fire. The jumping bonfire plant is the delight of children all over Obojima, and every village is sure to have one.
lootTables: Land of Hot Water Common Ingredients|ObojimaTallGrass

name: Kabutowari
entries: A dagger designed for piercing helmets.

name: Kakute
entries: {@i These rings each have two or three sharp, sturdy spikes. They are worn in sets.}

name: Kama
entries: A sickle.

name: Kama-yari
entries: A yari spear with an additional blade at a right-angle to the thrusting blade.

name: Kamadan's Snakes
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw. the creature takes 21 ({@damage 6d6}) poison damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful save.

entries.name: Special
entries: You require a Strength score of 17 or higher to use this weapon effectively, else your attacks have disadvantage.

entries.name: Special
entries: You require a Strength score of 17 or higher to use this weapon effectively, else your attacks have disadvantage.

name: Kanabō
entries: A heavy, two-handed maul, also known as a testubō.

name: Kanamuchi
entries: A long thin metal club.

name: Kangura Suzu
entries: {@i Fifteen bells of various sizes are hung by coiled brass wires in three tiers. The shapes of the bells are thought to take their inspiration from the fruits of the ogatama tree.}

name: Karuta
entries: Folding armor consisting of hexagonal plates linked by kusari mail.

name: Katana
entries: {@i A sword with a long handle and a high-quality blade. The blade is sharp on one side and slightly curved.}

entries.name: Special
entries: When wielded with one hand this weapon gains the finesse property.

entries.name: Special
entries: When wielded with one hand this weapon gains the finesse property.

name: Katana
entries: A longsword with a curved blade, carried by {@i samurai} and some {@i rōnin}.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you wield a katar, it fits around your hand, making it hard to disarm you of it. You have advantage on any ability check or saving throw to resist being disarmed of or dropping a katar you wield. However, it requires a bonus action to draw or stow a katar. While wielding a katar in a hand, you can't use that hand for anything else.

entries.name: Special
entries: A Large or smaller creature hit by a Ketch-All pole is {@condition restrained} until it is freed. A Ketch-All pole has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a {@dc 10} Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success.
When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a Ketch-All pole, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

name: Kevlar-Lined Coat
entries: Piercing damage that you take from firearms is reduced by 2.

name: Khopesh
entries: {@i The blade of this sword curves into a backward-facing sickle shape at the top half of its length.}

name: Khopesh
entries: A khopesh is a one-handed martial melee weapon that looks like a cross between a sword and a sickle. The long blade emerges from the hilt straight like a longsword, but the blade curves toward the end.

name: Khopesh
entries: {@i The blade of this sword curves into a backward-facing sickle shape at the top half of its length.}

name: Kikko
entries: {@i Kikko armor consists of small hexagonal plates connected by metal links and sewn over a canvas suit.}

name: Kikko
entries: Folding armor consisting of hexagonal plates linked by kusari mail.

name: Kloth Leech
entries: Kloth leeches are approximately the size of a handkerchief and come in a variety of colors. They tend to gather in groups made up of leeches of different colors, forming what resembles clumps of patchwork cloth. There are druidic communities in the Gale Fields who have learned to make entire garments from trained kloth leeches.

name: Knobble Leaf Seaweed
entries: There are many different kinds of seaweed on and around Obojima, most of which are quite tasty and nutritious, but none is more sought after than knobble leaf. Many cooks use knobble leaf in their soups and salads, and there are some witches and warlocks that use it for spells. Knobble leaf can be found washed up on the beaches of Obojima and growing in thick kelp beds along the sea floor surrounding the island.

name: Knobkerrie
entries: {@i A club with a weighty head balanced for throwing.}
A knobkerrie can be the subject of a {@spell shillelagh} spell but, if the weapon is thrown, the spell ends before it can affect the attack or damage rolls.

name: Knobkerrie
entries: {@i A club with a weighty head balanced for throwing.}
A knobkerrie can be the subject of a {@spell shillelagh|PHB} spell but, if the weapon is thrown, the spell ends before it can affect the attack or damage rolls.

name: Knuckle Dusters
entries: A knuckle duster is a simple melee weapon, usually made of metal or another hard material, worn around the knuckles of one hand. They deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage on a hit and have the Attached, Light, and Pugilist properties.

name: Kohachiwari
entries: {@i This weapon consists of a handle with a perpendicular spike affixed to one end. Kohachiwaris are ideal for finding gaps in armor or punching straight through it.}

name: Kojo Root
entries: You can find kojo root hanging within every shrine and temple on Obojima as it is considered good luck. Dried kojo root is also ground into a powder and used as seasoning in many dishes across the island.

name: Kojobi Fruit
entries: Almost every village has a couple of kojobi trees in it but they only fruit every two or three years. When a kojobi tree bears fruit it is a cause for celebration and everyone comes to take part in a Kojobi Festival where the abundant fruit is made into all kinds of dishes and beverages to be enjoyed by all.
lootTables: Land of Hot Water Uncommon Ingredients|ObojimaTallGrass

name: Kokiriki
entries: {@i An idiophone percussion instrument with small wooden blades connected by a rope. It often has handles at the ends. By waving the instrument, the strips collide to produce a percussive rhythm.}

name: Kopis
entries: This forward-curving shortsword is heavier along the end of the blade. This gives it significantly more cutting power than a typical shortsword, allowing it to be used like an axe.

name: Kozane
entries: {@i An armored cuirass and leggings made of lacquered scales tied together into a coherent protective material, sometimes stretched over wood or metal plates.}

name: Kozane dō
entries: Lamellar cuirass made of scales.

name: Kpinga
entries: {@i A one-handed multi-bladed weapon used like a knife or axe and balanced for throwing.}

name: Kpinga
entries: {@i A one-handed multi-bladed weapon used like a knife or axe and balanced for throwing.}

name: Kubb Set
entries: {@i Kubb is an outdoor game of skill in which players try to toss wooden batons to knock over a series of blocks.}

name: Kukri
entries: {@i This large dagger has a heavy blade, curved slightly toward its cutting edge. The weapon is designed for chopping.}

name: Kukri
entries: {@i This large dagger has a heavy blade, curved slightly toward its cutting edge. The weapon is designed for chopping.}

name: Kumade
entries: {@i A long pole with a trio of hooks at the end, like a claw. Resembling a pitchfork, his weapon is ideal for covert activities. When the hooks are attached to the top of a wall no more than 15 feet high, the pole can be climbed like a rope.}

entries.name: Special
entries: You can draw and throw up to 2 kunai as part of an attack when you take the attack action; for each thrown above the first you add an additional damage die.

entries.name: Special
entries: You can draw and throw up to 2 kunai as part of an attack when you take the attack action; for each thrown above the first you add an additional damage die.

name: Kusari
entries: {@i A heavy suit of chainmail consisting of a robe or long hauberk extending below the knees and cinched with a belt, plus a broad hood to protect the head, neck, and shoulders.}

name: Kusari
entries: Light mail armor.

name: Kusari-fundo
entries: A bludgeoning flail.

name: Kusarigama
entries: {@i This sickle-like weapon has a straight, perpendicular blade. A length of chain connects the bottom of the handle to a heavy weight.}

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon has a reach of 15 feet.

Because of the time required to draw back the entire length of the cord for another attack, you can attack only once with this weapon when you use an action, bonus action, or reaction, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make. This restriction does not apply when using the alternate (S) weapon property. The alternate (S) weapon property can only be used against targets within 5 feet.

If used as a double weapon, the primary end of the weapon can attack only once when you use an action, bonus action, or reaction, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make. (See {@book chapter 9|CompEquipMan|9|Double Weapon Fighting}.)

entries.name: Special
entries: This sickle-like weapon has a chain with a weight at the end. When you make a ranged attack by throwing the kusarigama you can pull the weapon back to your hand by the chain as part of the attack.

entries.name: Special
entries: This sickle-like weapon has a chain with a weight at the end. When you make a ranged attack by throwing the kusarigama you can pull the weapon back to your hand by the chain as part of the attack.

name: Kusarigama
entries: Manufacturing: {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}; 2 {@item Gold|XDMG|GP} materials; 4 hours.

Kusarigama are composed of a sickle attached to a heavy counterweight by a metal chain. They count as Monk weapons. They also have the Special: Counterweight property and the {@itemMastery Trip|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms|Trip Superior Strike}{@sup *}.

entries.name: Special: Counterweight
entries: While wielding a Kusarigama with two hands, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to attack with its counterweight. This attack has a reach of 10 feet and deals {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage on a hit. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of this attack, unless that modifier is negative.
{@note {@sup *}See {@loader Ryoko's Guide to the Yokai Realms|collection/Loot Tavern; Ryoko's Guide to Yokai Realms.json}}

name: Kusarigama
entries: A flail with a kama sickle on the end.

name: Kusarigama
entries: Kusarigama are martial melee weapons consisting of a sickle attached to a heavy counterweight by a metal chain. They deal 1d4 slashing damage on a hit, count as monk weapons, and have the Versatile (1d6) property. They also have the Special: Counterweight property. Due to the increased reach of this Special property, kusarigama count as having the Scourge property for the purposes of advanced weapon mastery

name: Kyoketsushoge
entries: {@i This is a large dagger with an additional hooked blade. A length of rope connects the bottom of the handle to a weighted ring or disk.}

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon has a reach of 15 feet.

Because of the time required to draw back the entire length of the cord for another attack, you can attack only once with this weapon when you use an action, bonus action, or reaction, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make. This restriction does not apply when using the alternate (P) weapon property. The alternate (P) weapon property can only be used against targets within 5 feet.

If used as a double weapon, the primary end of the weapon can attack only once when you use an action, bonus action, or reaction, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make. (See {@book chapter 9|CompEquipMan|9|Double Weapon Fighting}.)

name: Lajatang
entries: {@i A short polearm with two crescent shaped blades affixed perpendicularly to each end, tips pointed away from the haft.}

name: Lamellar
entries: This is a type of body armor made from small rectangular plates (scales or lamellar) of iron, leather, or bronze laced into horizontal rows.

name: Lamellar Coat
entries: {@i A common type of armor, the lamellar coat consists of bronze or iron plates laced together and sewn over a leather coat.}

entries.name: Special
entries: You have disadvantage when you use a lance to attack a target within 5 feet of you. Also, a lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

name: Lance, Silver
entries: You can wield this weapon in one hand while mounted.

entries.name: Wooden Melee Weapons
entries: When you make an attack roll with this Melee weapon and roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, the weapon splinters and is destroyed.

name: Land Warrior Armor
entries: Piercing damage that you take from firearms is reduced by 5. Slashing damage that you take is also reduced by 5.

It is designed to improve the connectivity and combat effectiveness of combat personnel in the army. Improvements include modernized body armor, a helmet with a mounted {@item flashlight|MH}, integrated communication systems, and a special eye monitor ({@item infrared goggles|MH}).

name: Lantern Shield
entries: This metal shield comes with a {@item hooded lantern|PHB} that can be hung from a hook on the shield's rim, allowing you to illuminate your path while keeping a hand free.

name: Large Carapace
entries: Used for {@book Leatherworking|KTKCG|17}.

name: Laser Claws
entries: When activated, these gloves project dazzling, razor-sharp claws from the fingertips, which can be used to shred a foe to ribbons.

name: Laser Claws
entries: When activated, this glove projects dazzling, razor-sharp claws from the fingertips, which can be used to shred a foe to ribbons. Usually, this weapon is wielded in pairs, making a light complement for deft two-weapon fighters.

name: Laser Greatsword
entries: The laser greatsword's two-handed hilt projects the longest fixed laser blade possible, which hisses and mists plasma in its wake. Naturally, this weapon leverages raw force more than agility, and can cleave any foe it catches in half.

name: Laser Halfsword
entries: This laser sword of shorter hilt and half-blade length is normally wielded in pairs, making a light complement for deft two-weapon fighters.

name: Laser Sword
entries: An elegant weapon, for a more enlightened age, the laser sword consists of a metal hilt which projects a fixed-length laser when activated. Its weightless blade makes for an agile, deadly weapon capable of cutting through many materials. The sword could even stop a blaster bolt, but alas, one would need precognition and superhuman reflexes to do so.

entries.name: Special
entries: Depending on this weapon's construction, it can deal force, necrotic, or radiant damage. Once the weapon is created, this damage type doesn't change.

name: Laser Sword
entries: An elegant weapon for a more enlightened age, the Laser Sword which projects a fixed-length laser from a metal hilt when activated. Its weightless blade makes for an agile weapon, capable of slicing through many materials. It could even stop a blaster bolt, but alas, one would need superhuman reflexes to intercept incoming plasma.

name: Lasso
entries: {@i A lasso is a knotted loop of rope used to entangle foes at short range.}

A Large or smaller creature hit by a lasso suffers no damage but is {@condition restrained} until it is freed. A lasso has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a {@dc 10} Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within reach on a success. A creature with an Intelligence of 7 or higher automatically succeeds at this check, knowing innately how to slip out of the tightened loop.
Alternately, the rope can be burst with a {@dc 17} Strength check or severed by dealing 2 slashing damage to it (AC 10). These options end the effect and permanently shorten the rope.

While you hold the other end of the rope to a {@condition restrained} target, you can use the rules for {@action Shove||shoving} a creature to pull the creature 5 feet towards you (instead of pushing it away) or to knock it {@condition prone}. If mounted and using a saddle, you can use your mount's characteristics when making these checks.

Making a lasso out of the end of a rope shortens the rope's effective overall length by 10 feet. A lasso cannot attack at a range longer than the rope's remaining length. Because it is not a weapon, it does not add your proficiency bonus when making attacks. When you use your action, bonus action, or reaction to lasso a target, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make. This does not apply to attacks on an already-restrained target when invoking the rules for {@action Shove||shoving} a creature, described above.

A Large or smaller creature hit by a lasso suffers no damage but is restrained until it is freed. A lasso has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a DC 10 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within reach on a success. Alternately, the rope can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check or severed by dealing 2 slashing damage to it (AC 10). These options end the effect and permanently shorten the rope.

While you hold the other end of the rope to a restrained target, you can use the rules for {@action shove|PHB|shoving} a creature to pull the creature 5 feet towards you (instead of pushing it away) or to knock it {@condition prone}. If mounted and using a saddle, you can use your mount's characteristics when making these checks.

Making a lasso out of the end of a rope shortens the rope's effective overall length by 10 feet. A lasso cannot attack at a range longer than the rope's remaining length. Because it is not a weapon, it does not add your proficiency bonus when making attacks. When you use your action, bonus action, or reaction to lasso a target, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make. This does not apply to attacks on an already-restrained target when invoking the rules for shoving a creature, described above.

name: Laughing Moss
entries: Laughing moss is well-known amongst naturalists and woodcutters, as it's fairly easy to find when you know what you're looking for. To find a patch of this moss is quite simple, as all you need to do is head to the woods and listen for the distinctive sounds of hearty laughter emanating from a campsite in the evening. Along with finding it in the wild, laughing moss is sold in special apothecaries around the island.

name: Layered Furs
entries: {@i Unhardened animal hides, when used in layers, provide significant protection to the wearer. Furs layered this way are used for armor in primitive societies or as ceremonial wear.}

name: Layered Hides
entries: {@i Multiple layers of heavy hides over a hardened leather underlayer. This heavy armor is very difficult to move in but provides serious protection without resorting to metal components.}

name: Lead Bullet
entries: The lead bullet is the default ammunition for every firearm, unless stated otherwise. The lead bullets of Luyarnha are alloyed with silver; they count as silvered for the purposes of overcoming resistances and immunities.

name: Lead Ingot
entries: Used for {@book Blacksmithing|KTKCG|12}.

name: Leaden Sling Bullet
entries: {@i This is the most common type of sling bullet, a simple lump or sphere of molded lead.}
These are normally referred to as just "sling bullets."

name: Leaden Sling Bullets (20)
entries: {@i This is the most common type of sling bullet, a simple lump or sphere of molded lead.}
These are normally referred to as just "sling bullets."

name: Leather Buckler
entries: A small, simple, and light {@item shield|PHB}. Wielding this shield increases your armor class by 1. You can benefit from only one shield at a time. You can hold items in the same hand as this light buckler, but any weapon wielded with the same hand has disadvantage on weapon attacks, and any {@action grapple|PHB|grappling} attempts with that hand are made with disadvantage.

name: Leather Corslet
entries: A close-fitting shirt of hardened leather with long sleeves.

name: Leather Jacket
entries: This armor is represented by a heavy leather biker's jacket.

name: Leather Scale Armor
entries: {@i A torso and shoulder covering made of stiff, overlapping scales of treated leather.}

name: Leather Scraps
entries: Used for {@book Leatherworking|KTKCG|17}.

name: Leather Shirt
entries: A lightweight garment of hardened leather, providing some protection to its wearer while allowing for great freedom of movement.

name: Legendary Branch
entries: Used for {@book Wand Whittling|KTKCG|16}.

name: Legendary Essence
entries: Used for {@book Alchemy|KTKCG|10}, {@book Enchanting|KTKCG|14}, {@book Scroll Scribing|KTKCG|15}, {@book Wand Whittling|KTKCG|16}.

name: Legendary Fresh Ingredient
entries: A fresh ingredient is something you harvest that can increase the quality of your food and sometimes provide supernatural boosts beyond mere satiation.
Used for {@book Cooking|KTKCG|13}.
Typically harvested from a monster of CR 16–20.

name: Legendary Magical Ink
entries: Magical ink that is used by Enchanters to create scrolls, made by rendering down magical alchemical ingredients.
Used for {@book Scroll Scribing|KTKCG|15}.

name: Legendary Meat
entries: Used for {@book Cooking|KTKCG|13}.

name: Legendary Parchment
entries: Used for {@book Scroll Scribing|KTKCG|15}.

entries.name: Rarity Benefit
entries: You gain a +3 bonus to the attack roll.

name: Legendary Reagent
entries: Used for {@book Alchemy|KTKCG|10}, {@book Poisoncraft|KTKCG|11}.

name: Length of String
entries: Used for {@book Wood Working|KTKCG|19}.

name: Lich Dust
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Strength)} for 24 hours. While the condition persists, the victim suffers from a flaking skin condition; the victim has disadvantage on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks made against humanoids that can see the victim's flaking "lich-like" skin. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each hour, ending the effect on itself with a success.

entries.name: Special
entries: You have disadvantage on attacks made with a bayonet that isn't attached to a crossbow. It takes an action to attach or remove a bayonet from a weapon.

name: Light Cannon
entries: Scaled-down versions of heavy cannons, light cannons trade sheer firepower for a faster rate of fire, greater density of stored {@item Light Cannon Round|DarkMatter|ammunition}, and more flexibility in mounting positions.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon deals double damage to objects and structures. This weapon deals double damage to objects and structures. Reloading this weapon requires 2 actions.

entries.name: Special
entries: You have disadvantage when you use a lance to attack a target within 5 feet of you. Also, a combat lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

entries.name: Wooden Ammunition
entries: Wooden ammunition is destroyed after hitting or missing a target.

name: Light Jousting Lance
entries: A jousting lance has a blunt end and is made to break away on impact. A creature wearing heavy armor has resistance to damage inflicted by a jousting lance.

entries.name: Special
entries: You have disadvantage when you use a jousting lance to attack a target within 5 feet of you. Also, a lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

name: Light Leather Armor
entries: Favored by gladiators and poor soldiers, this boiled leather armor offers minimal protection. It consists primarily of a thick, broad belt and one or two segmented arm and shoulder guards harnessed by leather straps.

name: Light Pick
entries: This weapon resembles a small pickaxe with a very long handle. It is equally as suited for digging as for throwing at an opponent.

name: Light Shuriken
entries: {@i Light shuriken are small, sharpened projectiles thrown at short range. They are often made from coins or similar scraps of metal.}

entries.name: Special
entries: Up to 6 light shuriken can be drawn as a single interaction with an object and held in one hand. This allows characters with Extra Attack or similar class features to throw multiple light shuriken in the same turn without a separate action to draw each one.

name: Light Tommybow (2)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Light Tommybow (3)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Light Tommybow (4)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Light Tommybow (5)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Light Tommybow (6)
entries: Tommybows are repeating crossbows that mirror the three types of normal crossbows: hand, heavy, and light. They are composed of vertically-stacked bows upon a crossbow's chassis, an unwieldy arrangement that reduces their effective range in comparison to their crossbow counterparts.

name: Light Undercover Shirt
entries: Piercing damage that you take from firearms is reduced by 2.

Designed for deep undercover work in which it's critical that the wearer not appear to be armed or armored, this garment consists of a T-shirt with a band of light protective material sewn in around the lower torso.

name: Light War Pick
entries: {@i The smallest version of a war pick, this weapon consists of a handle with a perpendicular spike affixed to one end. Picks are ideal for finding gaps in armor or punching straight through it.}

name: Light War Pick
entries: {@i The smallest version of a war pick, this weapon consists of a handle with a perpendicular spike affixed to one end. Picks are ideal for finding gaps in armor or punching straight through it.}

name: Light-Duty Vest
entries: Piercing damage that you take from firearms is reduced by 3.

A lightweight tactical vest designed for extended use by riot police and forces on alert for potential attack, this armor sacrifices a degree of protection for a modicum of comfort—at least compared to other tactical body armors.

name: Lightning Claw
entries: A gauntlet with three blades that are attached to the back of the hand and extend past the knuckles like long, sharp claws; each crackles with the thrum of the lightning unleashed when they slash apart opponents.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon deals an additional {@damage 2d4} lightning damage on a hit. You may roll the damage dice twice for this weapon and choose the higher result.

name: Lightning Coil
entries: This enormous transformer draws a similarly large amount of power and generates arcs of lightning thousands of feet long. Because the lightning discharges toward any nearby target, the lightning coil is actually omni-directional.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon deals double damage to shield points, but half damage (rounded down) to hit points. If this damage reduces a ship's shields points to 0, remaining damage is not subtracted from hit points.

name: Lionfish Poison
entries: Only the Lionfish King or one of his royal line is capable of producing this potent poison, and to procure even a tiny bit of it is a treasure indeed. Many who have tried to steal such a prize have wound up shark food or washed up on shore—poisoned by the very substance they sought to steal.

name: Lions Blume
entries: This carnivorous flower is characterized by a maw at the center of its array of honey-colored petals. Beekeepers consider the flower an invasive weed that devours bee populations. Lions blume grows in patches known as prides on the high moors of the Coastal Highlands. Each pride has its own lineage which tries to choke out other prides growing nearby. Brewers seek out lions blume because of the flower's milky sap as well as its "teeth."

name: Liturgical Mace
entries: {@i This mace has a large, hollow reservoir intended for holy water. The head of the weapon contains dozens of holes that are normally covered by an internal bladder. When the mace strikes a target, the impact jars and compresses the internal bladder, momentarily exposing the holes and dousing the target with liquid.}

If filled with {@item holy water (flask)|CompEquipMan|holy water}, the liturgical mace inflicts an additional {@damage 1d6} radiant damage against a fiend or undead. Likewise, {@item unholy water (flask)|CompEquipMan|unholy water} inflicts an additional {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage against a celestial. If filled with {@item defoliant (flask)|CompEquipMan|defoliant}, the liturgical mace inflicts an additional {@damage 1d6} acid damage against a plant creature.

A single flask of {@item holy water (flask)|CompEquipMan|holy water}, {@item unholy water (flask)|CompEquipMan|unholy water}, or {@item defoliant (flask)|CompEquipMan|defoliant} provides enough liquid to fill the mace, allowing the weapon to be used twice before it is empty. The internal components of the liturgical mace are too delicate to survive loading it with any harsh or volatile alchemies like {@item acid (vial)|CompEquipMan|acid} and {@item alchemist's fire (flask)|CompEquipMan|alchemist's fire}, or with poisons of any kind.

name: Liturgical Mace
entries: {@i This mace has a large, hollow reservoir intended for holy water. The head of the weapon contains dozens of holes that are normally covered by an internal bladder. When the mace strikes a target, the impact jars and compresses the internal bladder, momentarily exposing the holes and dousing the target with liquid.}

If filled with {@item Holy Water (flask)|PHB|holy water}, the liturgical mace inflicts an additional {@dice 1d6} radiant damage against a fiend or undead. Likewise, {@item Unholy Water (flask)|WorldofCollabris|unholy water} inflicts an additional {@dice 1d6} necrotic damage against a celestial. If filled with {@item defoliant|WorldofCollabris}, the liturgical mace inflicts an additional {@dice 1d6} acid damage against a plant creature.

name: Living Spud
entries: Every now and then, a spud pops out of the ground and begins a long meandering trek. Obojiman farmers call them "living spuds" and they are objects of curiosity and reverence. Wagons will stop on roads and people in crowded markets will make way to let a living spud trundle through. But whatever it is that animates these wayward potatoes, that magic is desired by potion brewers who will use even the smallest snip of a living spud to power their brews.

name: Lockjaw
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 12 hours. A creature that fails its saving throw by 5 or more is also unable to speak or use verbal spell components while the {@condition poisoned} condition persists. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each hour, ending the effect on itself with a success.

name: Lom Lom Dagger
entries: The short and angular blade of a lom lom dagger was designed for cleaving and quickly became a staple in most of Obojima's kitchens. Over time, the blade length grew longer and longer, and eventually the lom lom dagger made its way out of the kitchen and into the hands of adventurers, who favored it for its balance and accuracy when thrown.

name: Long Gun
entries: {@i A long-barrel version of the common musket, this weapon is suitable for hunting as well as warfare.}
This weapon loads ball or shot.

name: Long gun
entries: A long-barrel version of the common {@item musket|WorldOfCollabris}, this weapon is suitable for hunting as well as warfare. (Page 197)
This weapon loads ball or shot.

name: Long Haft
entries: Used for {@book Blacksmithing|KTKCG|12}.

name: Long Rifle
entries: {@i Rifles are very powerful, long-range firearms. They use bolt-action, falling block, or similar mechanisms, loading only one cartridge at a time. They come in normal, long, and carbine versions.}
A long rifle loads (high-power) cartridges.

entries.name: Wooden Ammunition
entries: Wooden ammunition is destroyed after hitting or missing a target.

name: Longspear
entries: {@i A longer spear with a haft still light enough for throwing.}

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Lovers Vine
entries: The lovers vine is actually two distinct vines that have developed a symbiotic relationship where one draws nutrients from the soil and the other provides a strong stem and ability to grasp and climb. Singly, neither vine provides a medicinal or magical effect, but when both are boiled together, their mixed properties are truly potent. Lovers vine can be found in most forests but it is especially fond of marshy areas.

name: Lucern Hammer
entries: {@i A polearm with a small hammer and spike combination at the head.}

name: Maca
entries: {@i The maca is a heavy wooden sword. Sharp pieces of obsidian, shark teeth, or other natural materials line the cutting edges.}

name: Maca
entries: {@i The maca is a heavy wooden sword. Sharp pieces of obsidian, shark teeth, or other natural materials line the cutting edges.}

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon deals double damage to plants and creatures of the plant type.

name: Macuahuitl
entries: A wooden club lined with prismatic blades of obsidian, capable of producing an edge sharper than high-quality steel razor blades, as such these weapons can cause serious lacerations.

entries.name: Special
entries: On a hit, this weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d4} slashing damage.

name: Macuahuitl
entries: A wooden club lined with prismatic blades of obsidian, capable of producing an edge sharper than high-quality steel razor blades, as such these weapons can cause serious lacerations.

entries.name: Special
entries: On a hit, this weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d4} slashing damage.

name: Magic Monk's Rice Wine
entries: Magic Monk's Rice Wine is a delicious and refreshing high-end spirit. Many who imbibe it say it stimulates the intellect and afterward their dreams are far more vivid. On each of the solstices, a delivery of Magic Monk's Rice Wine is handled by teams of spirits who mysteriously appear and distribute it to the taverns and temples of Obojima. Magic Monk's Rice Wine is brewed and distilled in some unknown location within the spirit realm.

name: Magitech Cannon
entries: AC: 17 | DT: 16 | HP: 30 | IT: 18 | Con: +2 | Ability: Dex,Int
Damage Immunities: Poison, Psychic

entries.name: Ball Shot
entries: {@atk r} range 180/360/1,440 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 4d8}) Bludgeoning damage. This shot has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against Hulls and kaiju at close range.

entries.name: Chain Shot
entries: {@atk r} range —/240/960 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 3d8}) Bludgeoning damage. This shot has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against masts and other tall, vertical structures (GM's discretion).

entries.name: Grape Shot
entries: {@actSave dex}, 90-foot Narrow Cone. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Piercing damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

name: Magitech Rifle
