The target of a sapping attack can use its reaction to protect its head, automatically negating any sapping attempts with such devices until the start of its next turn. It is therefore prudent to use this device only on targets that are {@quickref surprise|PHB|3||surprised} or otherwise prevented from using reactions.

If your sapping attack succeeds and the target is not reduced to 0 hit points, roll {@dice 2d6} to calculate a sapping number. If you have the {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|PHB|1|PHB} class feature, roll your Sneak Attack dice and add the result to your sapping number. If the number generated is equal to or higher than the target's remaining hit points, the target becomes {@condition unconscious}. Otherwise, the sapping roll has no effect.
A sapped creature regains consciousness after {@dice 1d4} hours or when it is healed for at least 1 hit point. At the Dungeon Master's discretion, other effects can also relieve this unconsciousness.
Constructs, oozes, plants, and undead are immune to sapping effects.

name: Sap
entries: {@i A sap consists of a heavy weight within a sleeve of leather or other padded material. Its purpose is to knock out creatures without killing them.}

Once per turn, you can use this weapon to attempt a sapping attack if you have not made (and will not make) a Sneak Attack that turn. A sapping attack requires a precise blow to a vulnerable portion of the target's head. The target of a sapping attack can use its reaction to protect its head, automatically negating any sapping attempts with such devices until the start of its next turn. It is therefore prudent to use this device only on targets that are surprised or otherwise prevented from using reactions.

If your sapping attack succeeds and the target is not reduced to 0 hit points, roll {@dice 2d6} to calculate a sapping number. If you have the Sneak Attack class feature, roll your Sneak Attack dice and add the result to your sapping number. If the number generated is equal to or higher than the target's remaining hit points, the target becomes {@condition unconscious}. Otherwise, the sapping roll has no effect.
A sapped creature regains consciousness after {@dice 1d4} hours or when it is healed for at least 1 hit point. At the Dungeon Master's discretion, other effects can also relieve this unconsciousness.
Constructs, oozes, plants, and undead are immune to sapping effects.

name: Sassone Leaf Residue
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 9} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Charisma, Intelligence, Wisdom)} for 10 minutes. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a success. Each failed saving throw, including the initial saving throw, inflicts 6 ({@damage 1d12}) poison damage.

name: Sasumata
entries: {@i A polearm used for nonlethal restraint, the blunt crescent crosspiece is used to deflect weapon attacks and hold attackers at range.}

entries.name: Special
entries: Once per turn, when you hit with this weapon you can force the target to succeed a Constitution saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier or be {@condition incapacitated} until the start of their next turn.

entries.name: Special
entries: On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d4} slashing damage at the start of their next turn.

name: Sax
entries: This short sword has a slashing edge and though these weapons are simply constructed, they are versatile and used by many raiders as their secondary weapon.
{@b Special.} unless magical, considered an {@i {@item inferior|ROTSSPGF}} weapon

entries.name: Credits
entries: Art and item designed by {@link Unknown|}. Please credit if you repost elsewhere.

name: Scale Armour
entries: This armour consists of a coat and leggings (and perhaps a separate skirt) of leather covered with overlapping pieces of metal, much like the scales of a fish. The suit includes gauntlets.

name: Scalefruit Rind
entries: Scalefruit are fist-sized fruits that are covered by a thick, scaly rind. Although the outside of a scalefruit is rather unappetizing, the interior is sweet and delicious, and is easily scooped after the fruit is cut in half. Many scalefruit farmers can be easily identified as they always carry a sharp cleaver and a metal scoop. Scalefruit trees are found along the coastline as they love sandy soil. Many seaside villages have their own creative versions of scalefruit drinks that they proudly serve to travelers.

name: Scales
entries: Used for {@book Leatherworking|KTKCG|17}.

name: Scatter Bullet
entries: {@i (requires a weapon with the {@itemProperty SGttEH:SpFr|SGttEH|spread fire} property)}

This bullet ignores the {@itemProperty SGttEH:SpFr|SGttEH|spread fire} property and is fired like a standard bullet. On a hit, the target takes your normal weapon damage and the bullet explodes, sending shrapnel flying in a 15-foot cone behind the target. Each creature in the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your Firearm save DC or take damage equal to your weapon damage.

name: Scatter Bullet
entries: When you make an attack using a weapon with the {@itemProperty SGttEH:SpFr|SGttEH24|Spread Fire} property, you can choose to use this ammunition. If you do, ignore the {@itemProperty SGttEH:SpFr|SGttEH24|Spread Fire} property and instead make an attack roll. On a hit, the target takes the weapon's normal damage, and the bullet explodes, sending shrapnel flying in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} originating from the target and extending away from you. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, a creature takes damage equal to your weapon damage.
Once it hits a target, the ammunition is destroyed.

name: Scattergun
entries: {@i This firearm usually has a tube magazine below the barrel. Shotshells or slugs are advanced into the ready position by a shuttle attached to a cranked windlass or a pump-action mechanism.}
These weapons load shotshells or slugs, or a combination thereof.

If loaded with a combination, keep track of the sequence of ammunition types to determine the effects of each shot. Disfavored ammunition can be ejected as unspent rounds in order to skip to a later-loaded ammunition type. This requires no additional effort in the firing process.

name: Scattergun
entries: This firearm usually has a tube magazine below the barrel. Shotshells or slugs are advanced into the ready position by a shuttle attached to a cranked windlass or a pump-action mechanism. It comes in normal and {@item Scattergun, short|WorldOfCollabris|short} versions.
These weapons load shotshells or slugs, or a combination thereof.

If loaded with a combination, keep track of the sequence of ammunition types to determine the effects of each shot. Disfavored ammunition can be ejected as unspent rounds in order to skip to a later-loaded ammunition type. This requires no additional effort in the firing process.

name: Scattergun, short
entries: This firearm usually has a tube magazine below the barrel. Shotshells or slugs are advanced into the ready position by a shuttle attached to a cranked windlass or a pump-action mechanism. It comes in {@item Scattergun|WorldOfCollabris|normal} and short versions.
These weapons load shotshells or slugs, or a combination thereof.

If loaded with a combination, keep track of the sequence of ammunition types to determine the effects of each shot. Disfavored ammunition can be ejected as unspent rounds in order to skip to a later-loaded ammunition type. This requires no additional effort in the firing process.

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Scissor
entries: {@i A rare gladiator weapon, the scissor is a metal tube with a small, fan-like blade extending from one end. The user reaches into the other end of the tube to grasp the handle, located at the end near the blade. The tube protects the user's forearm, allowing the wielder to block and quickly retaliate with a slash of the razor-sharp blade.}
You have advantage on any save or check you make to avoid being {@action Disarm|DMG|disarmed} of the scissor.

name: Scissor
entries: {@i A rare gladiator weapon, the scissor is a metal tube with a small, fan-like blade extending from one end. The user reaches into the other end of the tube to grasp the handle, located at the end near the blade. The tube protects the user's forearm, allowing the wielder to block and quickly retaliate with a slash of the razor-sharp blade.}
You have advantage on any save or check you make to avoid being disarmed of the scissor.

name: Scorcher
entries: Scorchers spit a narrow fan of flame from their mouths, normally with the intent of melting through the hulls of other ships or making them malleable enough to warp. Because of this uncouth design, scorchers trade range for the singular ability to bypass shield systems.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon produces a scorching fan of arcane energy which heats a ship's hull without affecting its shields. Shields do not block this weapon's damage.

name: Scorcher Fumes
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. While {@condition poisoned} this way, the creature is also {@condition blinded}. If the initial saving throw fails by 5 or more, the blindness becomes permanent, until cured by magic. If the initial saving throw is failed by 4 or less, the creature can attempt another saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a success.

name: Scorpion Venom
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 9} Constitution saving throw, taking 4 ({@damage 1d8}) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Scourge
entries: {@i This short, multi-lash whip is the sort used for administering punishments. It is more intimidating than effective when used as a weapon.}
Any creature wearing armor (or with natural armor) has resistance to the damage inflicted by this weapon.

name: Scourge
entries: This heavy metal-tipped whip is a martial weapon with the reach property. It deals {@damage 2d4} slashing damage on a hit. Due to its unwieldy nature, you have disadvantage when you use a scourge to attack a target within 5 feet of you.

name: Scourge
entries: {@i This short, multi-lash whip is the sort used for administering punishments. It is more intimidating than effective when used as a weapon.}
Any creature wearing armor (or with natural armor) has resistance to the damage inflicted by this weapon.

name: Screaming Arrow
entries: {@i The head of this arrow makes a screaming noise in flight.}
The sounds this arrow emits in flight can be easily heard within 100 feet of any point along its path.

name: Screaming Arrows (10)
entries: {@i The head of this arrow makes a screaming noise in flight.}
The sounds this arrow emits in flight can be easily heard within 100 feet of any point along its path.

name: Sculptor's Tools
entries: {@i This satchel contains chisels, mallets, files, and finishing polishes for sculpting statutes out of minerals (typically stone or clay) or applying decorative engraving to the mineral surfaces of walls, doors, and other edifices.}

With one minute of study, you can identify weak points in inanimate sculptures such that your successful attacks against them, or the successful attacks of others that you direct, are automatically critical hits.
Use sculptor's tools to modify a statute ({@dc 10}) or detect hidden messages in the designs engraved into a wall or similar surface ({@dc 20}).

name: Scumweed
entries: Whether it was brought by the Corruption or a local plant was mutated by it, scumweed has appeared on the corrupted coastlines of Obojima and is creeping further inland along sloughs and marshes that are affected by the encroaching Corruption. Scumweed is slimy and thick. Dried scumweed can even make hardy armor in a pinch and more than a few monsters and witches have been known to use it for precisely that purpose.

name: Scythe
entries: {@i A two-handed implement with a curled handle and a large, perpendicular, sickle-like blade.}

name: Scythe
entries: While it resembles the farm implement of the same name, this scythe is balanced and strengthened to focus tremendous force on the sharp point while allowing sweeping slashes with the blade edge.

entries.name: Weapon Technique
entries: {@optfeature Devastate|MATM}: When you land a critical strike with your scythe, you can use your bonus action to increase the damage of the scythe to {@damage 2d8} for that critical strike.

name: Scythe
entries: {@i A two-handed implement with a curled handle and a large, perpendicular, sickle-like blade.}

name: Sea Spawn Quills
entries: A creature subjected to this poison suffers 3 ({@damage 1d6}) poison damage and must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Sea Water
entries: Sea water is a staple in many potion brewing processes, but some master potion makers will demand seawater from certain areas around Obojima due to the particular elements, minerals, and energies present in the waters around that particular region. For those adventurers with a penchant for fibbery or a desire for easy money, a master can taste the difference in the waters around Obojima, so don't try to fool them with just any old sea water.
lootTables: Land of Hot Water Common Ingredients|ObojimaTallGrass

name: Seashell
entries: The beaches of Obojima are covered with different kinds of seashells. Many paths and walkways in the seaside villages are covered with simple white shells. Some of the more decorative ones are sold in shops.
lootTables: Land of Hot Water Common Ingredients|ObojimaTallGrass

name: Seax
entries: These fighting knives are too heavy to be thrown, but they boast long blades that can punch through leather and mail.

name: Secret Stone Sword
entries: Although it's not much of a secret nowadays, the magical stone known as feather rock, which is used to craft these stone swords, was once coveted and kept hidden by the Nakudama. Even though feather rock is now commonly used by potion brewers, and the craft of making one of these swords is fairly common, the name has stayed the same.

name: Segmented Plate
entries: This armor consists of a fitted metal chest piece worn with supple leather along with a helmet, pauldrons, gauntlets and greaves. Although it leaves the joints relatively unprotected, this armor provides good protection for the wearer's vital organs while leaving the wearer relatively unencumbered provided they are strong enough to manage its weight.

entries.name: Special
entries: When wearing this armor, you can add 3, rather than 2, to your AC if you have a Dexterity of 16 or higher.
If the wearer has a Strength score lower than 13, their speed is reduced by 10 feet.

name: Segmented Plate
entries: This armor consists of a fitted metal chest piece worn with supple leather along with a helmet, pauldrons, gauntlets and greaves. Although it leaves the joints relatively unprotected, this armor provides good protection for the wearer's vital organs while leaving the wearer relatively unencumbered provided they are strong enough to manage its weight.

entries.name: Special
entries: When wearing this armor, you can add 3, rather than 2, to your AC if you have a Dexterity of 16 or higher.
If the wearer has a Strength score lower than 13, their speed is reduced by 10 feet.

name: Sekkin
entries: {@i This lithophone consists of a small table of flat stones, each of which produces a different note when struck.}

name: Sentinel Blade
entries: A large, finely crafted broadsword wielded by a {@creature Knight-Sentinel of the Lightning Lord|FFESLL}. It has a pair of powerful bolt throwers built onto either side of the hilt, allowing the wielder to cut down foes both up close and at range.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon is considered adamantine for the purposes of resistance and immunity.

entries.name: Ranged Attack
entries: This weapon may also make ranged attacks in the same manner as a ranged weapon, which deal {@damage 2d4} force damage. It's ammunition is
If a ranged attack with this weapon is a critical hit it deals an additional 1d8 force damage.
When used as a ranged weapon it has the following additional properties:

name: Serpent
entries: {@i A common, standard-sized handgun of basic construction.}
This weapon loads ball or shot.

name: Serpent
entries: A common, standard-sized handgun of basic construction.
This weapon loads ball or shot.

name: Shadow Essence
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Strength)} for 2 minutes. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a success. If the creature fails 3 consecutive saving throws, no more attempts are allowed; the poison persists for the full duration.

name: Shadowroot
entries: This small, knobby root only grows where its black leaves are left in perpetual shadow. Once harvested, the root must be wrapped or sealed away from light or it will rapidly wither and rot.

name: Shang Gou
entries: {@i This weapon is the length of a traditional sword, but the end of the blade is curved forward into a sharp-pointed hook. An outward-facing crescent is set over the handle to guard the hand and to help with blocking, trapping, and slashing. Only the back of the blade, including the outer edge of the hook, is sharpened.}

entries.name: Special
entries: Using the {@action Attack} action, you can make a special melee attack with your sharrash to knock a creature prone. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the {@action Attack} action, this replaces one of them. The target must be no more than one size larger than you and must be within your reach. Instead of making an attack roll, you make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check contested by the target's Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check (the target chooses the ability to use). You succeed automatically if the target is {@condition incapacitated}. If you succeed, you knock the target {@condition prone}. This special attack has no effect on creatures that are Huge or Larger.

Talenta Halflings have disadvantage on all attack rolls and contested checks made with a sharrash if you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature and, while mounted, you ignore the heavy property and its damage is {@damage 4d4}.

name: Shashka
entries: A cavalry saber employed to great effect by mounted warriors, the shashka can be swung while on horseback in a repeated, looping downward arc. When riding through enemy ranks, a mounted warrior employs a one-handed, whirling swing, crisscrossing the rider's pommel to strike at enemies on foot on both sides in a downward double arc.

entries.name: Special
entries: A shashka can't be wielded with two hands while you are mounted.

name: Sheaf Arrow
entries: {@i This is the most common type of arrow used in combat, a sturdy shaft of reliable length, topped by a heavy broadhead or bodkin point.}
These are normally referred to as just "arrows."

name: Sheaf Arrows (20)
entries: {@i This is the most common type of arrow used in combat, a sturdy shaft of reliable length, topped by a heavy broadhead or bodkin point.}
These are normally referred to as just "arrows."

entries.name: Guillotine
entries: Immediately after hitting a target with the shears, if you have a free hand, you can use your reaction to pull the lever, snapping the blades together and dealing an extra {@damage 1d12} slashing damage to the target. If the triggering attack was a critical hit, you deal an extra {@damage 1d12} slashing damage. If this attack deals more than one-quarter of a creature's hit point maximum, you also {@table Losing Limbs|SGttEH|chop off one the creature's limbs (anything but the head) at the GM's discretion}. If this attack reduces a creature to 0 hit points, it is decapitated.

name: Sheep Dragon Wool
entries: The thick wool of the sheep dragon has been used by Obojimans for centuries as clothing, blankets, and even felt armor. Many villages have dyed sheep dragon wool in many vibrant colors. While most sheep dragons are domesticated, there are still wild sheep dragons roaming the grasslands of Obojima.

name: Shell
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

entries.name: Special
entries: As a bonus action, you can make a contested Strength check against a creature within range, moving the target to another unoccupied space within 5 feet of you on a success.

name: Shikiti
entries: The shikiti is designed as a tool to both scare off attacking monsters by creating an ear-rending screech when blown into it as well as deliver a painful sting to an enemy via a {@item blowgun needle|PHB|dart} emitted similarly to a {@item blowgun|PHB}, used to ward off bugcats due to their sensitive hearing. Its low damage potential renders it less useful against larger targets, however it has also found a home as an instrument, and alongside the {@item ululu|BloodInTheCompany} is a staple of Helviti musical tradition.

name: Shikomizue
entries: {@i This covert weapon appears to be a staff until the handle is separated from the haft, drawing forth a deadly sword blade.}

entries.name: Special
entries: While the sword is sheathed, the weapon can be used as a {@item quarterstaff|CompEquipMan}. Separated, the empty scabbard can be used as a {@item club|CompEquipMan} and is often wielded in the offhand.

entries.name: Special
entries: The scabbard of this sword may also be used as a weapon; when you are holding the shikomizue and its scabbard in each hand they are treated as light weapons. On a hit the scabbard deals {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Special
entries: The scabbard of this sword may also be used as a weapon; when you are holding the shikomizue and its scabbard in each hand they are treated as light weapons. On a hit the scabbard deals {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage.

name: Sho
entries: {@i A set of over a dozen slender reed pipes set in a metal base. This intricate instrument is said to imitate the call of the phoenix. The reeds sound on the player's inhaling breath as well as exhaling.}

name: Shoosuva Poison
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or become {@condition poisoned}. While {@condition poisoned}, the target is also {@condition paralyzed}. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a success.

name: Short Coach Gun
entries: {@i This variant of the scattergun has two breach-loading barrels that fire separately. The action of opening the breach ejects spent casings for easy and quick reloading.}
These weapons load shotshells or slugs, or one of each.

name: Short Haft
entries: Used for {@book Blacksmithing|KTKCG|12}.

name: Short Hooked Spear
entries: {@i The backward-facing hook on this short-hafted spear is designed for tripping opponents. Some versions have a smaller opposite hook on the butt end.}

name: Short Repeater
entries: {@i This firearm commonly uses a cylindrical rotating magazine, or a lever-action that feeds cartridges from an internal tube extending into the stock. Some use other, more exotic mechanisms. This weapon comes in normal and short versions.}
A short repeater loads (carbine) cartridges.

name: Short Scattergun
entries: {@i This firearm usually has a tube magazine below the barrel. Shotshells or slugs are advanced into the ready position by a shuttle attached to a cranked windlass or a pump-action mechanism.}
These weapons load shotshells or slugs, or a combination thereof.

If loaded with a combination, keep track of the sequence of ammunition types to determine the effects of each shot. Disfavored ammunition can be ejected as unspent rounds in order to skip to a later-loaded ammunition type. This requires no additional effort in the firing process.

name: Short Spear
entries: {@i A hafted weapon with a simple point at one end. A short spear is typically shorter and thicker than a javelin and may be suitable for off-hand use.}

entries.name: Wooden Ammunition
entries: Wooden ammunition is destroyed after hitting or missing a target.

name: Shortsword Gun
entries: {@i This weapon sees many configurations. It consists of a firearm of pistol caliber attached to a melee weapon of some sort. Because of the awkwardly-formed nature of these guns and their propensity for getting jarred repeatedly in melee combat, they are slightly less reliable than normal firearms.}

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wooden Melee Weapons
entries: When you make an attack roll with this Melee weapon and roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, the weapon splinters and is destroyed.

name: Shot
entries: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition}. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Shot Load
entries: {@i A shot load is a collection of tiny, round pellets that spread out as they leave the muzzle. Some shot loads consist of squared pellets held together in a cylindrical form with a mild adhesive that is vaporized as the shot is fired, allowing the pellets to spread.}
Shots with this ammunition apply the blast weapon property. Loads not in paper cartridge form include the weight of paper or cloth wadding strips.

name: Shot Loads (10)
entries: {@i A shot load is a collection of tiny, round pellets that spread out as they leave the muzzle. Some shot loads consist of squared pellets held together in a cylindrical form with a mild adhesive that is vaporized as the shot is fired, allowing the pellets to spread.}
Shots with this ammunition apply the blast weapon property. Loads not in paper cartridge form include the weight of paper or cloth wadding strips.

name: Shot Paper Cartridge Load
entries: {@i At this stage of development, ball and shot ammunition can be purchased in paper cartridge form. Paper cartridges are heavy paper packets containing both powder and load. They are easier to carry and a bit faster to load.}

You can load the barrel of a weapon from the Firearm 1 or 2 lists with a paper cartridge using an action or a bonus action, so long as the cartridge's contents match what the weapon can normally load (ball or shot). Paper cartridges otherwise function as ball or shot loads, described in this section, each with a contained charge of gunpowder.

name: Shot Paper Cartridge Loads (10)
entries: {@i At this stage of development, ball and shot ammunition can be purchased in paper cartridge form. Paper cartridges are heavy paper packets containing both powder and load. They are easier to carry and a bit faster to load.}

You can load the barrel of a weapon from the Firearm 1 or 2 lists with a paper cartridge using an action or a bonus action, so long as the cartridge's contents match what the weapon can normally load (ball or shot). Paper cartridges otherwise function as ball or shot loads, described in this section, each with a contained charge of gunpowder.

name: Shotel
entries: {@i The blade of this sword curves dramatically forward into a large hook. The weapon resembles an over-sized sickle.}

name: Shotel
entries: The curve of a shotel's blade allows you to reach around your opponent's {@item shield|PHB}.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you attack a creature wielding a {@item shield|PHB}, you gain a +2 bonus to the attack roll.

name: Shotel
entries: {@i The blade of this sword curves dramatically forward into a large hook. The weapon resembles an over-sized sickle. }

name: Shotshell Load
entries: {@i This large-bore cartridge contains multiple pellets instead of a single projectile. The pellets spread after leaving the weapon, hitting targets more easily or even hitting multiple targets.}
Shotshells can be loaded into coach guns, scatterguns, and their short versions, and into two of the mixed-use gun's barrels.
Shots with this ammunition apply the blast weapon property.

name: Shotshell Loads (Box of 50)
entries: {@i This large-bore cartridge contains multiple pellets instead of a single projectile. The pellets spread after leaving the weapon, hitting targets more easily or even hitting multiple targets.}
Shotshells can be loaded into coach guns, scatterguns, and their short versions, and into two of the mixed-use gun's barrels.
Shots with this ammunition apply the blast weapon property.

name: Shreef Oil
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Dexterity, Strength)} for 10 minutes.

name: Shtra Ta
entries: The Shrta Ta is a long pole with a lengthy, swordlike spear tip extended along its length, held in place with either bars or other fixings. This weapon was designed to give the user additional reach as well as flexibility in close quarters when held by the base or near the middle, alternating being used as a staff and a polearm. Its use is similar to that of a {@item glaive|PHB}, but is less top-heavy and unbalanced, whilst being much heavier overall, used by the Helviti in caves and canyons to hunt {@creature winged spider|BloodInTheCompany|Winged Spiders} on their home turf.

name: Shudo
entries: A light crossbow.

entries.name: Special
entries: You can draw and throw up to 3 shuriken as part of an attack when you take the attack action; for each thrown above the first you add an additional damage die.

entries.name: Special
entries: You can draw and throw up to 3 shuriken as part of an attack when you take the attack action; for each thrown above the first you add an additional damage die.

name: Shuriken
entries: A small bladed throwing weapon with rotational symmetry.

name: Shuriken
entries: Shuriken, also known as throwing stars, are martial ranged weapons—several sharp spikes or blades set in a circular pattern, usually around a central ring. They deal 1d4 piercing damage on a hit, count as monk weapons, and have the Finesse, Light, and Thrown (range 20/60) properties.

name: Siangham
entries: {@i This simple thrusting weapon resembles a short, metal arrow with a sharp head and a handle instead of fletching at the base.}

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Silk-Backed Coin Mail
entries: Made of silver coins from conquered nations and backed by a layer of quilted red wormsilk, these hauberks are typically awarded to soldiers, mercenaries, and generals with conspicuous valor in the campaign that conquered the land from where the coins originated. While wearing this armor, you have resistance to piercing damage from nonmagical weapons. If the piercing damage is from a critical hit, the armor loses this property until you spend a short rest repairing it (no special tools or check required).

name: Silver Ingot
entries: Used for {@book Blacksmithing|KTKCG|12}.

name: Silver Scraps
entries: Used for {@book Jewelcrafting|KTKCG|22|Jewelcrafting}.

name: Singularity Emitter
entries: Less a blaster in the conventional sense, and more a stripped-down Dark Matter engine designed to rip a contained hole in the universe, the singularity emitter is a singularly destructive weapon. After being fired, however, the weapon must cool down, venting exceptional amounts of heat to maintain a stable Dark Matter core.

entries.name: Special
entries: When this weapon hits a target, each creature within 10 feet of the target is pulled up to 5 feet toward it.

name: Skates
entries: While wearing skates, you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} from slippery ice and automatically pass Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) checks to avoid have the {@condition Prone} condition on ice. You move at double your normal {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} while on ice, but you have a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 5 feet off the ice.

name: Skathári Warclub
entries: True to their nature, skathári warriors prefer simple, straightforward weapons, such as their traditional warclubs. These clubs are fitted with a row of large spikes for punching through invertebrate shells and discouraging huge predators.

name: Skathári Warclub
entries: True to their nature, skathári warriors prefer simple, straightforward weapons, such as their traditional warclubs. These clubs are lined with a row of spikes for punching through invertebrate shells and discouraging huge predators.

name: Skeggøx (bludgeoning)
entries: This versatile handaxe has a wide cutting surface suitable for use in battle but the haft can be gripped directly behind the head to work with wood. Additionally, the weapon can be turned over to strike enemies with the hammer end.
{@b Special.} grants advantage when using woodworking or carpentry tools

entries.name: Credits
entries: Art and item designed by {@link Unknown|}. Please credit if you repost elsewhere.

name: Skeggøx (slashing)
entries: This versatile handaxe has a wide cutting surface suitable for use in battle but the haft can be gripped directly behind the head to work with wood. Additionally, the weapon can be turned over to strike enemies with the hammer end.
{@b Special.} grants advantage when using woodworking or carpentry tools

entries.name: Credits
entries: Art and item designed by {@link Unknown|}. Please credit if you repost elsewhere.

name: Skiprock
entries: These polished, perfectly weighted, and somewhat magical stones are prized by halflings, for if thrown properly by a user they ricochet off one target to strike a second.

entries.name: Weapon Technique
entries: {@optfeature Skipping Strike|MATM}: If a ranged weapon attack with a skiprock hits its target, it ricochets toward another target of your choice within 5 feet of the original target. You immediately make a second attack roll with disadvantage. Skiprocks can be used as {@item sling|phb} bullets, but cannot make ricochet shots when used as ammunition unless a user is proficient in both weapons. Any bonus damage or other effects only apply to the first target hit.

name: Skis
entries: While wearing skis, you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} from deep snow and move at double your normal {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} while going downhill in snow. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saves and checks while wearing skis, except those related to moving through snow.

name: Sleeping Merchant
entries: Known for its naturally soporific effects, the sleeping merchant got its name through its use by traveling traders who traditionally drink its dried blossoms as a tea after a busy day of hocking their wares. This water lily can be identified by the nodding white blossom under a leafy umbrella. The sleeping merchant only grows in certain ponds and lakes which has made attempts to grow sleeping merchant plants in other bodies of water impossible. Thus, the demand for this plant is high among the tea vendors of Obojima.

name: Sleeping Weed
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must make a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Dexterity)} for 5 minutes. While {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned} this way, the subject is "slowed." Its speed is halved, it takes a 2-point penalty to AC and Dexterity saving throws, and it can't use reactions. On its turn, it can use either an action or a bonus action, not both. Regardless of the creature's abilities or magic items, it can't make more than one melee or ranged attack during its turn. If the creature attempts to cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action, roll a {@dice d20}. On an 11 or higher, the spell doesn't take effect until the creature's next turn, and the creature must use its action on that turn to complete the spell. If it can't, the spell is wasted. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself after 2 successful saving throws.

name: Slingshots
entries: Slingshots are simple ranged weapons comprising an elasticated material strung between a Y-frame brace.

name: Slingshots
entries: Slingshots are simple ranged weapons comprising an elasticated material strung between a Y-frame brace.

name: Slug Load
entries: {@i This large-bore cartridge contains a single, heavy projectile.}
Slugs can be loaded into coach guns, scatterguns, and their short versions, and into two of the mixed-use gun's barrels.
Shots with this ammunition apply the deadly weapon property.

name: Slug Loads (Box of 50)
entries: {@i This large-bore cartridge contains a single, heavy projectile.}
Slugs can be loaded into coach guns, scatterguns, and their short versions, and into two of the mixed-use gun's barrels.
Shots with this ammunition apply the deadly weapon property.

name: Slungshot
entries: {@i A short length of rope knotted around a stone or metal weight at one end. This weapon evolved from the weights used to throw mooring lines between ships and shore. Sailors and dock workers often carry these weapons in their pockets. A slungshot can be swung forcefully, and an experienced wielder can make attacks with it from unexpected angles.}
A slungshot has a loop at the other end that can be attached to (or detached from) the wielder's wrist with an action. If the slungshot is so attached, it cannot be {@action disarm|DMG|disarmed}.

name: Slungshot
entries: {@i A short length of rope knotted around a stone or metal weight at one end. This weapon evolved from the weights used to throw mooring lines between ships and shore. Sailors and dock workers often carry these weapons in their pockets. A slungshot can be swung forcefully, and an experienced wielder can make attacks with it from unexpected angles.}

entries.name: Special
entries: A slungshot has a loop at the other end that can be attached to (or detached from) the wielder's wrist with an action. If the slungshot is so attached, it cannot be disarmed.

name: Smoke Arrow
entries: {@i A thin wrap of an alchemical material encases the shaft of this arrow behind the head.}

You may spend a bonus action to knock this arrow and dip the point into an active fire source prior to shooting, causing the material to smoke vigorously. The arrow trails smoke as it flies and creates a 5-foot cube of smoke wherever it hits. The smoke dissipates in {@dice 1d4} rounds, or until dispersed by a wind of at least 10 mph. Smoke arrows are each crafted to emit a specific color of smoke, useful for signaling.

name: Smoke Arrows (10)
entries: {@i A thin wrap of an alchemical material encases the shaft of this arrow behind the head.}

You may spend a bonus action to knock this arrow and dip the point into an active fire source prior to shooting, causing the material to smoke vigorously. The arrow trails smoke as it flies and creates a 5-foot cube of smoke wherever it hits. The smoke dissipates in {@dice 1d4} rounds, or until dispersed by a wind of at least 10 mph. Smoke arrows are each crafted to emit a specific color of smoke, useful for signaling.

name: Snaerispear
entries: These short, javelin-like spears can be hurled great distances by means of a "throwing string," a leather strap affixed to the mid-point of the spear shaft. This allows the snaerispear to deal more damage when thrown than in melee.

name: Snap Vine Sap
entries: Snap vines are carnivorous plants with a thick central stalk and many thinner grasping, hook-like tendrils that they use to ambush unsuspecting birds and small rodents. The sap is a viscous orange-red fluid.

name: Sniper Rifle
entries: An instrument of ranged precision, the Sniper Rifle can take shots from distant, nearly invisible ranges.

name: Snow Goggles
entries: These thick glasses are set with lenses of smoky glass, preventing snow blindness.

name: Snow Visor
entries: These thick bone or wood visors are bound to the head and are constructed with a narrow slit for the wearer's eyes. Creatures wearing snow visors have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to snow blindness but have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks relating to sight.

name: Snowshoes
entries: While wearing snowshoes, you can ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} from deep snow. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saves and checks while wearing snowshoes.

name: Sodegarami
entries: {@i Called a "sleeve tangler," this polearm's barbs are designed to catch in the enemy's clothing.}

name: Sovnya
entries: {@i A rugged polearm with a slashing blade that curves slightly, terminating in a sharp point.}

name: Spark Plug
entries: Spark plugs are used by potion makers to add in a small charge of magic, just enough to be a catalyst for a specific reaction. Most Obojimans still have no idea what these strange items are, let alone where they come from but the rangers and rogues who do keep the information to themselves.
lootTables: Land of Hot Water Uncommon Ingredients|ObojimaTallGrass

name: Spear
entries: {@i A hafted weapon with a simple point at one end. A short spear is typically shorter and thicker than a javelin and may be suitable for off-hand use.}

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wooden Melee Weapons
entries: When you make an attack roll with this Melee weapon and roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, the weapon splinters and is destroyed.

name: Special Response Vest
entries: You have resistance against piercing damage you take from firearms. Slashing damage that you take is also reduced by 2.

Built like the {@item tactical vest|MH}, but incorporating groin and neck protection as well as a ceramic plate over the chest, this armor provides additional protection in battles against heavily armed opponents.

name: Spetum
entries: {@i An elongated spear with outward-facing angled blades, designed to attack formations of foes. The weapon can wound as it is thrust forward and as it is drawn back toward the wielder.}

name: Spider Venom
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 9} Constitution saving throw or take 2 ({@damage 1d4}) poison damage.

name: Spiked Armor Gauntlet
entries: {@i A metal gauntlet formed of overlapping plates, the type used with metal armors. This version has spikes on the knuckles and the back of the hand.}

Any suit of {@filter heavy armor or medium armor|items|type=!treasure (gemstone);!treasure (art object);heavy armor;medium armor;!renaissance;!treasure (coinage);!modern;!futuristic|rarity=none} with the {@item armor spikes|CompEquipMan} attachment (other than {@item hide armor|CompEquipMan|hide}, {@item layered hides|CompEquipMan}, or {@item layered furs|CompEquipMan}) comes with two of these. The listed cost and weight are for buying and carrying the spiked gauntlet separately.

name: Spiked Cesti
entries: A spiked cestus is a simple melee weapon worn around the knuckles of one hand that deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage on a hit and has the Adaptable (piercing), Attached, and Pugilist properties.

name: Spiked Cestus
entries: Manufacturing: {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}; 1 {@item Gold|XDMG|GP} materials; 2 hours.

Spiked Cesti are thick leather straps worn around the knuckles of one hand, armed with sharp spikes to puncture targets. They also have the {@itemMastery Flurry|RyokoGuideToYokaiRealms|Flurry Superior Strike}{@sup *}.
{@note {@sup *}See {@loader Ryoko's Guide to the Yokai Realms|collection/Loot Tavern; Ryoko's Guide to Yokai Realms.json}}

name: Spiked Chain
entries: {@i This chain has various weights and sharp protrusions at strategic points along its length. It is designed to entangle foes.}

entries.name: Special
entries: If you have the Dual Wielder feat or the Two-Weapon Fighting style, you can wield a spiked chain as two one-handed, light weapons that each deal {@damage 1d6} piercing damage. The spiked chain loses the reach property when wielded in this way.

entries.name: Special
entries: You have disadvantage when you use a spiked chain to attack a target within 5 feet of you. Spiked chains are notoriously difficult to control, so even proficient wielders must exercise extreme caution when employing spiked chains in close quarters.

name: Spiked Chain
entries: The spiked chain can easily wrap around a foe or an object to bring them to the ground.

entries.name: Weapon Technique
entries: {@optfeature Unhand|MATM}: When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn with a spiked chain, you can attempt to disarm a weapon or another item from a target's grasp. Make an attack roll with advantage contested by the target's Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. If you win the contest, the attack causes no damage or other ill effect, but the target drops the item. You can only use this technique once per turn.

entries.name: Weapon Technique
entries: {@optfeature Sweep|MATM}: When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn with a spiked chain against a large or smaller creature, you can sweep an enemy's legs out from under them with your spiked chain.If the attack hits, the attack causes no damage or other ill effect, but the creature must make a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone}. You can only use this technique once per turn.

name: Spiked Chain
entries: {@i This chain has various weights and sharp protrusions at strategic points along its length. It is designed to entangle foes.}

name: Spiked Knuckle Dusters
entries: A knuckle duster is a simple melee weapon, usually made of metal or another hard material, worn around the knuckles of one hand. They deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage on a hit and have the Attached, Light, and Pugilist properties.

name: Spiked Shield
entries: This shield is outfitted with formidable metal spikes. A creature who attempts to {@action grapple|PHB} you takes {@damage 1d4} piercing damage, plus an extra {@damage 1d4} piercing damage at the start of each of their turns while {@action grapple|PHB|grappling} you. Additionally, attacks made with this shield deal an extra {@damage 1d4} piercing damage on a hit.

name: Spiked Shield
entries: Encompassing a variety of different types from targe to pavise, these spiked shields all feature one or many spikes in their defensive design. Wielding a spiked shield increases your Armor Class by 2. You can benefit from only one shield at a time.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you take the Attack action and attack with a light melee weapon that you're holding in one hand, you can use a bonus action to attack with this shield if you're holding it in the other hand as if it was also a light melee weapon and you are two-weapon fighting. On a hit it deals {@damage 1d4} piercing damage, you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative.

name: Spiked Shield
entries: A small shield with a spike protruding from the front. The spiked shield can be used as a light weapon in your off-hand that deals {@damage 1d4} piercing damage. You may also use this as a template for a Dwarven Buckler-Axe, which instead deals slashing damage.

entries.name: Weapon Technique
entries: {@optfeature Spiked Thrust|MATM}: When a creature makes a melee weapon attack against you, you can use your reaction to attempt to parry the blow, increasing the shield's AC bonus to +2 for that attack. If the attack misses, you can make a melee weapon attack with your shield against the attacker as part of that reaction, dealing {@damage 1d4} piercing damage. You must declare your intention to use your spiked thrust before the DM rolls the die.

name: Spindle Leg Spider Webs
entries: The silky, strong webs of the spindle leg spiders are woven in thick hammock-like nets under bushes and in dense tall grass. The webs are strong enough to catch small animals which the spindle web spiders wrap and hang in their silken larder. Spindle leg spiders are found in forests, under large bushes, and in areas where the grass grows tall.

name: Spirit Naga Venom
entries: A creature subjected to this poison takes 31 ({@damage 7d8}) poison damage.

name: Spirit Root
entries: Spirit root is called such because many Obojimans believe that if you leave it under your pillow at night it will remove any bad spirits—especially those who plague children with nightmares. Some villagers also believe that spirit roots are where dara come from. Spirit root can be found growing out from between rocks in and around mountainous and seemingly desolate areas.

name: Spirit Tea
entries: There are many fine teas to be tried all over Obojima, but only a few are legendary. One such tea is made by the master tea blender, Chisuay. It is said that Chisuay leaves his body and brews this tea in the Spirit Realm, then, through powerful magic, he brings this delicate spiritual brew back into the Material Plane. Spirit tea can only be found at Chisuay's teahouse.
lootTables: Land of Hot Water Uncommon Ingredients|ObojimaTallGrass

name: Spontoon
entries: {@i A short-bladed polearm with a small, straight crosspiece. This weapon is often decorative or ceremonial.}

name: Sprig of Mistletoe
entries: {@i This sprig of mistletoe is worn on a string or thong around the neck. It is the most recognizable symbol of druidic power.}

name: Spring
entries: Springs come in various sizes from different machines. Because of their spiral shape and ferrous material, they are prized by magic users to channel energies into spells and potions. Merchants who deal in arcana are always looking for springs found within the ruins of those who came before.
lootTables: Land of Hot Water Uncommon Ingredients|ObojimaTallGrass

name: Sprite Spit
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or become {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. If its saving throw result is 5 or lower, the {@condition poisoned} target falls {@condition unconscious} for the same duration, or until it takes damage, or until another creature takes an action to shake it awake.

name: Squid Ink
entries: Squid ink is highly sought after by calligraphers and fine clothiers as the ink makes for excellent writing ink and a rich, colorful dye for the finest clothes. Some chefs also prize the ink to add some color and a unique flavor to their soups and dishes. Squid ink can be found in the many different kinds of squid that live in the waters surrounding Obojima.

name: Stabilized Crossbow Bolt
entries: {@i This bolt is crafted with a target tip and some small fletching.}

When using this ammunition, both the crossbow's range increments are increased by a distance equal to half the weapon's normal range increment. When firing a stabilized crossbow bolt, apply a –1 penalty to the damage roll.

name: Stabilized Crossbow Bolts (20)
entries: {@i This bolt is crafted with a target tip and some small fletching.}

When using this ammunition, both the crossbow's range increments are increased by a distance equal to half the weapon's normal range increment. When firing a stabilized crossbow bolt, apply a –1 penalty to the damage roll.

name: Stake
entries: {@i This weapon is a short, sturdy wooden stick sharpened at one end. The other end is typically flat, suitable for hammering the shaft into the ground or into the heart of a resting vampire.}

name: Standard Carbine
entries: As its name might suggest, the standard carbine is the standard-issue blaster for all Hegemony and Coalition troops, which by default makes it one of the most pervasive weapons in the galaxy. Some soldiers praise the weapon's accuracy and durability, while others decry its difficult-to-control automatic fire; on the battlefield, however, there's no questioning this weapon's efficacy.

name: Standard Carbine
entries: As its name might suggest, the Standard Carbine is the standard-issue blaster for all Hegemony and Coalition troops, which makes it one of the most pervasive weapons in the 'Verse. Spacers of all stripes employ it for its compact size and superb accuracy.

name: Standard Carbine
entries: As its name might suggest, the Standard Carbine is the standard-issue blaster for all Hegemony and Coalition troops, which makes it one of the most pervasive weapons in the 'Verse. Spacers of all stripes employ it for its compact size and superb accuracy.

name: Standard Carbine
entries: As its name might suggest, the Standard Carbine is the standard-issue blaster for all Hegemony and Coalition troops, which makes it one of the most pervasive weapons in the 'Verse. Spacers of all stripes employ it for its compact size and superb accuracy.

name: Star Hammer
entries: From a sphere mounted at the end of its handle, the star hammer emits a half-dozen radiant jets, appearing like spikes or candle flames. The force through these jets sounds like a gong on particularly hard impacts.

name: Starbuster
entries: Scorchers spit a narrow fan of flame from their mouths, normally with the intent of melting through the hulls of other ships or making them malleable enough to warp. Because of this uncouth design, scorchers trade range for the singular ability to bypass shield systems.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon produces a scorching fan of arcane energy which heats a ship's hull without affecting its shields. Shields do not block this weapon's damage.

name: Starknives
entries: Starknives are martial melee weapons; three to five double-edged blades set on a central handle that are most effective as thrown weapons but can also be used for close combat. They deal 1d4 piercing damage on a hit, can count as a monk weapon, and have the Adaptable (slashing), Finesse, Light, Thrown (range 20/60), and Thrown Versatility (1d6) properties.

name: Starstone
entries: Starstone is a glittering crystalline rock that came from an ancient comet that broke up over Obojima long ago and scattered fragments across the island. Nakudama sages talk of this event in their sacred books, saying it was an auspicious omen, and ever since that time, the hunt for fragments of this Starstone has been undertaken. Starstone is very rare and is found lying on the ground or embedded in the earth. It is identified by its signature teardrop shape and magical shimmer.

name: Steel Blowgun Needle
entries: {@i This is a lightweight needle, about six inches in length, used as blowgun ammunition. A puff of downy feather attached to one end allows the projectile to be fired from a blowgun with a firm blast of lung power. Steel needles are often used to deliver toxins, being dipped in a vial of poison or other substance just before firing.}
These are normally referred to as just "blowgun needles."

name: Steel Blowgun Needles (50)
entries: {@i This is a lightweight needle, about six inches in length, used as blowgun ammunition. A puff of downy feather attached to one end allows the projectile to be fired from a blowgun with a firm blast of lung power. Steel needles are often used to deliver toxins, being dipped in a vial of poison or other substance just before firing.}
These are normally referred to as just "blowgun needles."

name: Steel Chain (2ft)
entries: Used for {@book Tinkering|KTKCG|18}, {@book Blacksmithing|KTKCG|12}.

name: Steel Ingot
entries: Used for {@book Blacksmithing|KTKCG|12}.

name: Steel Jaws
entries: Because they have no hands, worgs cannot wield weapons in the same way that most player characters can. However, worgs can wield a specially designed Martial Melee weapon called "Steel Jaws." Only {@race Worg|FoEQuickstone|Worgs} can wield Steel Jaws, fitting as they do over a Worg's teeth. A Worg cannot use its Bite trait while it is wielding Steel Jaws.

name: Stench Kow Breath
entries: This is a far-reaching inhalant; a creature is also subjected to this poison if it enters within 10 feet of the poison's primary 5-foot area or starts its turn within 10 feet of that primary area. A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} until the start of the its next turn. On a successful saving throw, the creature is immune to this scent and the scent of all {@creature stench kow|VGM|stench kows} for 1 hour.

name: Stiletto
entries: {@i This long, narrow blade is designed to slip between the plates of armor or the links of chain mail.}

name: Stiltto
entries: {@i This long, narrow blade is designed to slip between the plates of armor or the links of chain mail.}

name: Stone Rake
entries: Settlers use stone rakes to remove rocks and other obstructions from the soil prior to planting or building structures. Though stone rakes aren't built with combat in mind, more than a few settlers have fended off wild animals with them.

name: Stone Sling Bullet
entries: {@i In a pinch, a slinger can make use of appropriately-sized stones in the place of bullets.}
Stones cost nothing to collect but are less effective due to their irregular shapes; they apply a –1 penalty to the weapon's damage roll.

name: Stone Sling Bullets (20)
entries: {@i In a pinch, a slinger can make use of appropriately-sized stones in the place of bullets.}
Stones cost nothing to collect but are less effective due to their irregular shapes; they apply a –1 penalty to the weapon's damage roll.

name: Stone Yklwa
entries: A {@item Stone Yklwa|CompEquipMan|common variant} of the Yklwa, this weapon has a blade of chipped stone or obsidian instead of steel.

name: Stonesteel
entries: Made from an alloy of steel and crystalline stone, this unique form of plate armor represents the height of dwarven metallurgy. It consists of overlapping, interlocking plates that cover the entire body, and it includes gauntlets, heavy leather boots, and a helmet. Stonesteel is heavy and somewhat unwieldy but offers superior protection to standard plate. Donning and doffing stonesteel armor takes twice as long as normal plate armor.

name: Striped Toadstool
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must make a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Intelligence, Wisdom)} for 1 hour. While {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned} this way, the creature has trouble focusing its vision and distinguishing hallucinations from reality; it treats everything farther than 20 feet away as {@table Screen; Obscured Areas|ScreenDungeonKit|lightly obscured}. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each minute, ending the effect on itself with a success.

name: Submachine Gun
entries: Firing lighter, easier to control rounds, the Submachine Gun is an effective alternative to larger automatic weapons.

name: Subtle Tessen
entries: {@i An iron fan, or war fan, comes in two forms: a butterfly-shaped sheet of metal attached to a handle, used to deflect enemy attacks, or a true folding fan that has heavy iron ridges and other components, allowing it to be spread as a defensive weapon, or swung closed for a heavier impact.}

entries.name: Special
entries: This subtle version appears to be nothing more than an ordinary fan, perhaps slightly oversized, unless the item is handled or scrutinized from a very close distance.

name: Summer Smoke Ring Festival Pipe
entries: An elegantly crafted pipe inlaid with silver accents and a pearl stem. The pipe is worth 1 gold piece and grants advantage on ability checks using it.

Pipes are made of clay or wood and used for inhaling the smoke of burning leaves of pipe-weed. A character that has proficiency with a pipe practises the art of smoking and likely has some skill at blowing smoke-rings. Smoking a pipe can aid you in efforts at introspection, and in friendly chatting with fellow practitioners of the art.
If you are proficient with pipes, you can spend one use of pipe-weed and at least one hour smoking your pipe to gain inspiration. You cannot use a pipe again in this way until you finish a long rest.

name: Sun Shroom
entries: Discovered by the wizard known as Karoglin the Sleepless, the sun shroom allows those who consume it to stay awake for long periods of time. Overuse can lead to extended bouts of uncontrollable laughter and eventually deep restless sleep. Sun shroom has a briny taste and is most commonly consumed by mixing it in tea. Sun shrooms tend to grow near the roots of trees in the Wandering Forest, a fact that has led some to speculate that energizing mushrooms are what keep the trees on the move.

name: Sunfire Canister
entries: A canister containing enough ammunition for 4 shots.

name: Sunstaff
entries: This long staff, forked at its end near a prominent gemstone, is a blaster in its own right. When used in expert hands, the sunstaff can bludgeon, trip, and strike foes as a quarterstaff, only to be squeezed in both hands to fire a burst of hot plasma seconds later.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon can also be used as a {@item quarterstaff}.

name: Survival Knife
entries: A survival knife comes with a small {@item compass|MH} attached to the handle or pommel, and a hollow handle, which allows storing small items, such as some waterproof matches, a fishing string, or a piece of paper.

name: Svirfneblin Poison
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The secrets of crafting this poison are well-known to {@creature Deep Gnome (Svirfneblin)||svirfneblin}. If using the optional {@variantrule Formulas|CompEquipMan} rule, acquiring the formula requires interacting with {@creature Deep Gnome (Svirfneblin)||svirfneblin}.

name: Swallow
entries: {@i Similar in configuration to a double scimitar, the swallow uses two heavier, broader falchion blades and a shorter handle.}

name: Swarm Pistol
entries: This handheld blaster, styled much like a repeater, has a wickedly fast automatic fire, capable of spewing dozens of rays in seconds. The most dexterous users might even find it possible to use one in each hand.

name: Swarm Pistol
entries: This handheld blaster, styled much like a {@item Repeater|DarkMatter24}, has a wickedly fast automatic fire, capable of spewing dozens of rays in seconds. Dexterous users might even find it possible to use one in each hand for a dazzling spectacle of plasma bolts.

name: Swarm Pistol
entries: This handheld blaster, styled much like a {@item Repeater|ValdaGunslingerExtras}, has a wickedly fast automatic fire, capable of spewing dozens of rays in seconds. Dexterous users might even find it possible to use one in each hand for a dazzling spectacle of plasma bolts.

name: Swarm Pistol
entries: This handheld blaster, styled much like a {@item Repeater|ValdaSpire24Extras}, has a wickedly fast automatic fire, capable of spewing dozens of rays in seconds. Dexterous users might even find it possible to use one in each hand for a dazzling spectacle of plasma bolts.

name: Sword Cane
entries: {@i This covert weapon appears to be nothing more than a simple cane until the handle is twisted and the thin sword blade withdrawn from its length.}
The cane portion (sheath) can be wielded as a {@item club|CompEquipMan}, whether or not the sword has been drawn from it.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon is actually a hollow sheath for a rapier or specially-made shortsword. The rapier or special shortsword is not included in the price of the sword cane; rapiers have their listed cost in the Player's Handbook and a specially fitted shortsword costs 20 gp instead of 10 gp but otherwise uses the normal statistics for a shortsword. Each sword cane can only accommodate the weapon it was created for. While sheathed in a sword cane, the weapon is completely hidden and only a DC 20 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check made while holding and inspecting the cane reveals its nature as a sheath. The cane is made of strong hardwood and can be used as a weapon itself, using the listed statistics.

name: Sword Cane
entries: {@i This covert weapon appears to be nothing more than a simple cane until the handle is twisted and the thin sword blade withdrawn from its length. }

name: Swordbreaker
entries: A dagger with a series of hooked, horizontal notches opposite the blade, used to catch and entrap the opponent's weapon.

name: Tactical Vest
entries: You have resistance against piercing damage you take from firearms.
The standard body armor for police tactical units, this vest provides full-torso protection in the toughest flexible protective materials available.

name: Taiko
entries: {@i A generic style of drum built in various sizes and for various uses.}

name: Tail Spike
entries: {@i This is a ring or plate that straps onto a creature's tail and locks or ties into place. The device boasts sharp protrusions that can be whipped about to great effect.}

entries.name: Special
entries: This device is only usable by creatures with long tails that are prehensile or partially-prehensile. Applicable player character races include lizard folk, tabaxi, tiefling, and any others designated by the Dungeon Master. A creature armed with tail spikes may attack with the weapon using a bonus action as though armed with a light off-hand weapon. Do not add your ability modifier to damage when attacking with tail spikes, even if you have a trait or feature that would allow you to do so with an off-hand weapon.

name: Tail Spikes
entries: {@i This is a ring or plate that straps onto a creature's tail and locks or ties into place. The device boasts sharp protrusions that can be whipped about to great effect.}

This device is only usable by creatures with long tails that are prehensile or partially-prehensile. Applicable player character races include lizard folk, tabaxi, tiefling, and any others designated by the Dungeon Master. A creature armed with tail spikes may attack with the weapon using a bonus action as though armed with a light off-hand weapon. Do not add your ability modifier to damage when attacking with tail spikes, even if you have a trait or feature that would allow you to do so with an off-hand weapon.

name: Talharpa
entries: A musical instrument with two to four strings similar to a lyre and played with a bow.

name: Talwar
entries: {@i This weapon resembles a scimitar, except that it has a thinner, elongated blade. In some versions, the blade widens near the tip for greater momentum when swinging.}

name: Talwar
entries: {@i This weapon resembles a scimitar, except that it has a thinner, elongated blade. In some versions, the blade widens near the tip for greater momentum when swinging.}

name: Tanegashima
entries: The matchlock rifles used by Chinushi Nobunaga's forces that allowed him to gain military superiority over the other {@i daimyō}.

entries.name: Special
entries: Talenta Halflings ignore the heavy property and its damage is increased to {@damage 3d4}.

name: Tangle Weed
entries: Fisherfolk are at constant war with these plants, which snare fishing lines. It is commonly believed that tangle weed is not natural but is a species bewitched by fish folk to torment land dwellers who come too close to the water. This invasive species can be found clumped together throughout the Shallows.

name: Tanned Leather
entries: Used for {@book Leatherworking|KTKCG|17}.

name: Tapper Sack
entries: A tapper sack is a simple tool and weapon used by farmers. At the end of a fine, yet sturdy, braided cord is a simple bag which has been filled with sand. Although it's not very flashy, in the hands of a skilled adventurer this humble weapon packs quite a punch.

name: Taser Gun
entries: A taser gun fires two small barbed darts intended to puncture the skin and remain attached to the target, then it applies a high-voltage, but low-current electrical charge. When you hit a creature, it takes {@damage 1d4} lightning damage and it must make a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 15}) or be {@condition paralyzed} until the end of your next turn. While the target is within range, on each of your turns for the next 4 rounds you can use your action to deal {@damage 1d4} lightning damage and maintain the target {@condition paralyzed}. You can only have one creature under the taser gun's effects, and on each of its turns it can use an action to make a Constitution check. On a success, it removes the darts and is no longer {@condition paralyzed}.
A taser gun must be recharged using a {@item battery|MH} after five shots.

name: Tattoo Artist's Tools
entries: {@i This set of tools includes a variety of needles and inks as well as ointments and various treatments used to create tattoos on the skin of animals and humanoids.}

If you are a spellcaster, or working with a spellcaster, you can use these tools to inscribe a {@item spell scroll} into the skin of a living creature, creating a temporary tattoo. Each limb and the torso of a humanoid is large enough for a single spell. The costs and time needed for inscription are the same as for an equivalent {@item spell scroll}. Humanoids can see and read the {@item spell scroll||spell scrolls} on their own bodies when not covered by heavy clothing; such creatures can employ the tattoos as normal {@item spell scroll||spell scrolls} if they otherwise able to use {@item spell scroll||spell scrolls}. Another spellcaster can read uncovered {@item spell scroll} tattoos if the decorated creature is cooperative, {@condition restrained}, or {@condition unconscious}.
Use tattoo artist's tools to identify tattooing techniques or origins ({@dc 10}) or create tattoos with hidden meanings or messages ({@dc 20}).

name: Tears of the Moon
entries: On certain nights, a cloud in the Spirit Realm passes into the physical world and is struck by the moon's rays which crystallizes it into a glittering mist known as moonbreath. On rare occasions, moonbreath may form into larger crystals known as tears of the moon, that fall to the earth to be discovered by a lucky traveler.

name: Tedate
entries: Rectangular wooden or iron-plate shield.

name: Tegha
entries: {@i This large, curved sword was designed for use as an executioner's weapon. It must be wielded with two hands.}

name: Tegha
entries: {@i This large, curved sword was designed for use as an executioner's weapon. It must be wielded with two hands.}

name: Tekko
entries: {@i This small, blunt handle isn't much longer than needed to grip it in one hand. This variation of the yawara has a crescent of metal guards the grip, often bearing dull spikes or knobby protrusions.}

name: Tekko Kagi
entries: {@i A set of long claw blades that extend perpendicularly from a handle, protruding from between the user's fingers.}

entries.name: Special
entries: Donning or doffing this glove-like weapon requires an action and you may hold another object in the same hand as the tekkō-kagi.

name: Temple Sword
entries: Also called a sickle sword, the blade ends in a crescent-shaped curve.

name: Terinav Root
entries: Once applied, this contact poison remains effective for 1 month before becoming inert. A creature subject to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned (Dexterity)} for 10 minutes. While {@condition lesser poisoned|CompEquipMan|poisoned} this way, the creature's movement speeds are reduced by 10 feet. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of each minute, ending the effect on itself with a success.

name: Tessen
entries: {@i An iron fan, or war fan, comes in two forms: a butterfly-shaped sheet of metal attached to a handle, used to deflect enemy attacks, or a true folding fan that has heavy iron ridges and other components, allowing it to be spread as a defensive weapon, or swung closed for a heavier impact.}

name: Tessen
entries: A war fan, used for striking and deflecting attacks

entries.name: Special
entries: If you are proficient with martial weapons, you may increase your Armor Class by 1 while wielding a tessen. If you attack with the tessen, you lose this bonus and regain it at the start of your next turn. You can benefit from only one tessen at a time.

name: Tessen
entries: Tessen are martial melee weapons consisting of folding fans reinforced with wood or metal. The edges contain razor-sharp blades, but they can also be used as bludgeoning weapons when closed. They deal 1d4 slashing damage on a hit, count as monk weapons, and have the Adaptable (bludgeoning), Finesse, and Light properties. They also have the Special: Fan Shield property.

name: Tetherhooks
entries: A tetherhook is a martial melee weapon. It is comprised of a hook attached to a chain or strap

name: Tetherhooks
entries: A tetherhook is a martial melee weapon. It is comprised of a hook attached to a chain or strap

name: Thermal Lance
entries: When a button on this metal tube is pressed, a persistent, foot-long blue stream of flame erupts from its end, scorching those it touches. Though this tool was fashioned for mining asteroids for precious minerals, it has become a favorite (albeit eccentric) choice of weapon for avia-ra warriors.

name: Thermal Lance
entries: When a button on this metal tube is pressed, a persistent, foot-long blue stream of flame erupts from its end, scorching those it touches. Though this tool was fashioned for mining asteroids for precious minerals, it has become a favorite (albeit eccentric) choice of weapon for avia-ra warriors.

name: Thever Fumes
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. While {@condition poisoned} this way, the creature is also {@condition blinded}. If the initial saving throw fails by 5 or more, the blindness becomes permanent, until cured by magic. If the initial saving throw is failed by 4 or less, the creature can attempt another saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a success.

name: Thever Paste
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 10 minutes. While {@condition poisoned} this way, the creature is also {@condition blinded}. If the initial saving throw fails by 5 or more, the blindness becomes permanent, until cured by magic. If the initial saving throw is failed by 4 or less, the creature can attempt another saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself with a success.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you make an attack with this weapon, you can make another attack with it as a bonus action.

name: Thri-Kreen Venom
entries: A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the target is also {@condition paralyzed} while {@condition poisoned} this way. The {@condition poisoned} target can repeat the saving throw on each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Throwing Bandolier
entries: This is a quick access bandolier that can old weapons with the {@itemProperty T||thrown} property. It can be configured to hold 2 {@item javelin|PHB|javelins}, {@item handaxe|PHB|handaxes}, or {@item light hammer|PHB|light hammers}, or 4 {@item dagger|PHB|daggers} or {@item dart|PHB|darts}. Weapons held in it can be drawn as part of making an {@action attack|PHB} with them without using an {@action Use an Object|PHB|object interaction} to draw them as long as you have a free hand to draw them.

name: Throwing Dagger
entries: {@i The blade and handle of this dagger are flat, without quillons or crossguard, and balanced for throwing. Because of this shape, carrying and drawing multiples of this weapon is easy.}

Up to 3 throwing daggers can be drawn as a single interaction with an object (or a single action) and held in one hand. This allows characters with Extra Attack or similar class features to throw multiple throwing daggers in the same turn (using the other hand) without having to use a separate action to draw each one.

name: Throwing Dagger
entries: {@i The blade and handle of this dagger are flat, without quillons or crossguard, and balanced for throwing. Because of this shape, carrying and drawing multiples of this weapon is easy.}

Up to 3 throwing daggers can be drawn as a single interaction with an object (or a single action) and held in one hand. This allows characters with Extra Attack or similar class features to throw multiple throwing daggers in the same turn (using the other hand) without having to use a separate action to draw each one.

name: Thunder Cannon Ammo
entries: Ammunition for the {@item Thunder Cannon|KTKCG}.

name: Thunder Hammer
entries: A large warhammer that's closer to a maul and hums with the energy it contains, letting out powerful blasts of thunder when struck against a target.

entries.name: Special
entries: On a hit, this weapon deals an additional {@damage 2d4} thunder damage.

name: Thunderbox
entries: {@i A heavy handgun with five barrels arranged in a cluster, all of which fire simultaneously. The weapon is very expensive and time-consuming to load and use at full effect.}

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon loads ball or shot. If loaded with multiple ammunition types, the weapon's shots use the majority ammunition's statistics.

Reduce the weapon's damage to {@damage 2d8} piercing if fired with only three or four barrels loaded, or {@damage 1d8} piercing if fired with only one or two barrels loaded. Likewise, reduce the weapon's misfire rating to equal the number of barrels loaded when fired.
